## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node. It is versioned, cascaded, tagged and published.
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto never parses `target` and never builds; it records where the bytes go.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish.

## Layers

| Layer | Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |

## Two routes, one executor

```
local:  derive_unreleased_decision (untagged versions)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
```

- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

## Run envelope and state (`release.rs`)

- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.

## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)

- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup falls back to paging the release list (`provider/forge.rs`).

- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. - A changed decision gets a new ADR with `Status: Supersedes N`. The old file moves to `docs/adr/superseded/` with `Status: Superseded by M`. Agents do not load that folder.
- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.
# Release execution

The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node. It is versioned, cascaded, tagged and published.
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto never parses `target` and never builds; it records where the bytes go.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish.

## Layers

| Layer | Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |

## Two routes, one executor

```
local:  derive_unreleased_decision (untagged versions)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
```

- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

## Run envelope and state (`release.rs`)

- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.

## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)

- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup falls back to paging the release list (`provider/forge.rs`).

## Verification tiers

- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns.
- Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`.
- Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`.
# Package identity

How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Dual-manifest package: one directory with both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json` (e.g. a napi addon); one package, two release identities.
- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.

## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)

| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo:foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |

- `parse` treats text before the first `:` or `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare.
- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
- `PackageId` is display and selector only; `Package::key()` (the package's directory) is the stable identity, and default tags use the native `name()` (ADR 11).
- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
  - Different names never match.
  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
- Why bare is a wildcard: a dual-manifest package has one name in several ecosystems and one version, so `foo` must reach `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` alike.

## Resolving ambiguity

Do not change `matches`. A polyglot workspace can hold `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens.

- Lookups use `PackageId::resolve_unique`: collect every match, error on two or more. Callers: `aggregate::resolve_target_package` (changeset entries) and `commands/status.rs`.
- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: two linear passes over the rules in declaration order, prefixed rules first, then bare. It never sorts the rules. A bare rule that reaches a promoted name is an `AmbiguousName` error, using `ResolvedConfig::promoted_siblings`.
- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.

## Loading a workspace

`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):

1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids, then names promoted into several ecosystems are recorded as `promoted_siblings`.
4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.

## Platform packages in code

| Step | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` |
| Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` |
| Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` |
| List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` |
| Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) |
| Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform |

- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.
name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, moon and the .prototools toolchain, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: local requires this checkout; release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's
      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  verification:
    description: >-
      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml). One of: require = a failed
      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never
      run the unverified asset); skip = do not verify, warn, and use the asset. Releases built
      before the first attested release carry no attestation, hence the fallback default.
    required: false
    default: 'fallback'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: ${{ inputs.verification }}
        GITHUB_ACTION_REF: ${{ github.action_ref }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/install-callisto.sh" # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.
# proto plugin: installs the callisto CLI from GitHub release assets.
# .prototools: [plugins.tools] callisto = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/orin-dx/callisto/main/proto/callisto.toml"
name = "callisto"
type = "cli"

[platform.macos]
archs = ["aarch64"]
download-file = "callisto-{arch}-apple-darwin.tar.gz"
exe-path = "callisto"

[platform.linux]
archs = ["x86_64"]
download-file = "callisto-{arch}-unknown-linux-{libc}.tar.gz"
exe-path = "callisto"

[install]
download-url = "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto/releases/download/callisto@{version}/{download_file}"

[resolve]
git-url = "https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto"
version-pattern = "^callisto@(?<major>\\d+)\\.(?<minor>\\d+)\\.(?<patch>\\d+)(?:-(?<pre>[0-9A-Za-z.-]+))?$"

## Rules

- An ADR records an architecturally significant decision that had a credible alternative.
- `Proposed` until the PR that implements it merges, then `Accepted`.

- Every reason cites a source (commit, PR, historical doc). If none exists, write "Reason not recorded".
- Behaviour belongs in `docs/specs/`; coding rules belong in `AGENTS.md`.
# Release execution

The types that make a release run safe to crash and rerun, and how the two release routes share them. Behavior: [`docs/specs/release.json`](../specs/release.json). Operator guide: [`docs/releasing.md`](../releasing.md). Decisions: ADRs [2](../adr/0002-committed-decision-is-release-authority.md), [3](../adr/0003-reruns-adopt-landed-effects.md), [4](../adr/0004-ecosystem-tools-publish-and-own-auth.md) and [7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Package: a dependency-graph node. It is versioned, cascaded, tagged and published.
- Artifact: the bytes of one *(package, version, target)*, declared by `[[release.artifact]]`. It has no version, tag or changelog of its own. Callisto never parses `target` and never builds; it records where the bytes go.
- Product package: `[release].product-package`. Every artifact slot uploads to the product's one GitHub Release, even when another package built the bytes (`ArtifactSlotId.package`).
- Decision: the package and version roster (`ReleaseDecisionV1`).
- Intent: the decision plus the source snapshot, every operation with its prerequisites, and the artifact slots, sealed by a digest (`ReleaseIntentV1`).
- Operation: one effect on one provider, identified by package, version and role: registry publish, platform publish, tag, forge release (draft), artifact upload, forge publish.

## Layers

| Layer | Crate | Contents |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Authorities | `callisto-model` (MIT) | Run envelope and execution state (`release.rs`), observations and evidence (`release_observation.rs`), transition table (`release_transition.rs`) |
| Derivation and execution | `callisto-graph` | Decisions (`commands/release_decision.rs`), intent derivation (`commands/release/derive.rs`), local route (`commands/release/local.rs`), executor (`commands/release_execution.rs`), provider adapters (`commands/release/provider/`) |
| Entry points | `callisto-cli` | `commands/release.rs`: `release`, `release plan`, `release artifact-manifest`, `release execute` |

## Two routes, one executor

```
local:  derive_unreleased_decision (untagged versions)  -> plan_local_release -> intent
CI:     committed decision file, or --package over plan_version -> release plan -> intent -> build -> release execute
both:   intent -> ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new -> execute_release -> ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state
```

- `plan_local_release` is the one derivation behind both `callisto release --dry-run` and the real run.
- `ci_release_route` sends a workspace with artifact slots or platform builds to the CI route before anything runs.
- `expand_selection` (group members) and `require_dependencies_selected` (unselected unreleased dependencies) apply to both routes.

## Run envelope and state (`release.rs`)

- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1` is one run's identity: orchestration revision, release-source revision, intent digest, artifact-manifest digest.
- `ReleaseRunEnvelopeV1::new` is its only constructor. The source revision and intent digest are read from the intent, so a caller cannot assert them; the constructor cross-checks the rest against the intent before any effect.
- `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::new(intent, envelope)` is the only way to start a state, so no state exists without a validated envelope.
- The state is never persisted or loaded. Every run starts with every operation `Pending`.
- `ReleaseReceiptV1::from_state` builds the receipt from the state alone: the envelope plus the evidence each operation recorded on success. Nothing re-observes providers after the effects.

## Observation and evidence (`release_observation.rs`)

- `ProviderObservationV1` is `Absent`, `Exact { evidence }`, `Conflict { reason }` or `Indeterminate { cause }`. Reasons and causes are closed enums.
- `ProviderEvidenceV1` is closed and per role: registry version, git tag peeled commit, forge release tag and draft flag, artifact size and sha256.
- `ReleaseOperationObservationV1::new` rejects evidence whose shape does not belong to the operation's role; deserialization goes through it too.
- Proof tokens: `AbsentProof` is minted only from `Absent`, `ExactEvidence` only from `Exact`.
- `execute_release` observes each operation once before its effect: exact is adopted, absent is performed then confirmed, anything else stops the run before the effect.

## Transition table (`release_transition.rs`)

`transition` is the only function that computes an `OperationState`; `ReleaseExecutionStateV1::apply` is the only mutator. The whole legal edge set:

| From | Event | To |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pending | `Attempt { AbsentProof }` | Attempting |
| Pending | `ObservedExactBeforeEffect { ExactEvidence }` | AlreadySatisfied |
| Attempting | `Confirmed { ExactEvidence }` | Published |
| Attempting | `EffectFailedAndAbsent { AbsentProof }` | Failed |
| Pending or Attempting | `Blocked { reason }` | Blocked |

- Any other pair is an `InvalidTransition`.
- `Attempting` is unreachable without a proof of absence.
- `Published` (our effect landed) stays distinct from `AlreadySatisfied` (it existed before this run).

## Forge ordering

- A GitHub release is created as a draft, assets upload to the draft, and publication is a separate last operation that depends on every upload. A published release can be immutable and refuse new assets.
- GitHub's release-by-tag endpoint omits drafts, so the forge lookup falls back to paging the release list (`provider/forge.rs`).

## Verification tiers

- Fault-injection simulator (`commands/release_simulator.rs`): drives the real `execute_release` against an in-memory provider world, crashing at every provider call and injecting every provider outcome, with each rerun starting fresh. It asserts that a receipt is issued only when every effect really landed and only from state, that no landed effect is re-issued, that no effect lands before its prerequisites, and that each scenario converges within three clean reruns.
- Provider contract tier: fake providers replay captured real responses from `testing/fixtures/providers/`; `TOOL_SHAPES` in `crates/callisto-cli/tests/common/release_harness.rs` rejects flags a fake does not know, and `provider_flag_contract_tests.rs` checks each emitted flag against the real tool. `just provider-fixtures` re-captures and `just provider-contract` checks shapes live; both need the network and are outside `just ci`.
- Wire shapes: decision, intent, envelope and receipt each carry a `SCHEMA_VERSION`; the execution state has no wire shape. `callisto schema --type release-receipt` publishes the receipt schema, guarded by `crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs`.
# Package identity

How the workspace names packages, why bare names match across ecosystems, and where platform packages are wired in. Behavior: [`docs/specs/workspace.json`](../specs/workspace.json). Config keys: [`docs/config.md`](../config.md). Platform ownership decision: [ADR 7](../adr/0007-platform-packages-owned-through-optional-dependencies.md).

## Terms

- Dual-manifest package: one directory with both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json` (e.g. a napi addon); one package, two release identities.
- Co-located platform manifest: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in the same directory as its owner's `Cargo.toml`.
- Attached platform package: an `os`+`cpu` `package.json` in its own directory, owned via another package's `optionalDependencies`.

## `PackageId` (`crates/callisto-model/src/identity.rs`)

| Form | Example | `ecosystem()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Bare(name)` | `foo`, `@scope/foo` | `None` |
| `Prefixed { ecosystem, name }` | `cargo:foo`, `npm/@scope/foo` | `Some(e)` |

- `parse` treats text before the first `:` or `/` as a prefix only when `Ecosystem::from_prefix` knows it, so `@scope/foo` stays bare.
- `display_name` renders a prefixed id as `ecosystem/name`.
- `PackageId` is display and selector only; `Package::key()` (the package's directory) is the stable identity, and default tags use the native `name()` (ADR 11).
- `matches` is a weak "could be the same package" relation, not equality:
  - Different names never match.
  - A bare id matches any id with the same name, in either direction: bare is an ecosystem wildcard.
  - Two prefixed ids match only when their ecosystems are equal.
- Why bare is a wildcard: a dual-manifest package has one name in several ecosystems and one version, so `foo` must reach `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` alike.

## Resolving ambiguity

Do not change `matches`. A polyglot workspace can hold `cargo:foo` and `npm:foo` as separate packages; ambiguity is resolved where a lookup happens.

- Lookups use `PackageId::resolve_unique`: collect every match, error on two or more. Callers: `aggregate::resolve_target_package` (changeset entries) and `commands/status.rs`.
- `[[package]]` rules use `config::resolve::resolve_package_config`: two linear passes over the rules in declaration order, prefixed rules first, then bare. It never sorts the rules. A bare rule that reaches a promoted name is an `AmbiguousName` error, using `ResolvedConfig::promoted_siblings`.
- `[[package-set]]` is a fallback applied in `ManifestWalkResolver::build` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/walk.rs`) only when no `[[package]]` rule matched. Patterns (`config/pattern.rs`) are globs over the name with an optional ecosystem prefix, tested against every ecosystem the package has a manifest in.

## Loading a workspace

`Workspace::load` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/lib.rs`):

1. `config::load` reads `callisto.toml` (absent means empty) and calls `config::resolve`, which does all validation and defaulting. Callers holding a `RawConfig` in memory call `resolve` directly.
2. `ManifestWalkResolver::build` discovers projects, assigns ids (`IdentityIndex`), attaches platform packages and applies per-package config.
3. `GroupTable::resolve` binds group members to ids, then names promoted into several ecosystems are recorded as `promoted_siblings`.
4. The tag index is built lazily, on the first `Workspace::tags` call.

## Platform packages in code

| Step | Where |
| --- | --- |
| Find candidates outside the npm workspace globs | `ProjectLocator::projects_and_platform_candidates` |
| Attach a platform to its single owner, or warn | `platform_owners` in `walk.rs` |
| Look up a platform's owner by the platform's own npm name | `IdentityIndex::platform` |
| List an owner's attached platforms (co-located ones excluded) | `IdentityIndex::attached_platforms` |
| Write the owner's version into platform manifests and pin `optionalDependencies` | `platform_version_writes` in `commands/version.rs` (version and snapshot) |
| Publish each platform before its owner | `commands/release/derive.rs`: one `PlatformPublish` operation per attached platform |

- A `PlatformPublish` operation carries the owner's package id and version, so it passes the intent's check that every operation belongs to a decision entry, and each one is a prerequisite of the owner's npm `RegistryPublish`.
- It gets no tag, forge or artifact operation of its own; it publishes by directory.
- Release identities come from `release_package_ids` (`commands/release_decision.rs`): one per canonical manifest, using that manifest's own name, so a dual-manifest package with different Cargo and npm names releases under both.
name: 'Setup Callisto Environment'
description: 'Sets up Rust toolchain, Cargo cache, moon and the .prototools toolchain, and Callisto CLI'
inputs:
  source:
    description: 'Where to obtain Callisto: local requires this checkout; release jobs must use local.'
    required: false
    default: 'auto'
  version:
    description: >-
      Version tag of Callisto to install. Default 'latest' installs the release this action's
      own invocation is pinned to (github.action_ref resolved against callisto@ tags), falling
      back to the newest published release when that ref is unset or unresolvable.
    required: false
    default: 'latest'
  verification:
    description: >-
      Attestation verification of the prebuilt release asset (gh attestation verify, repo
      orin-dx/callisto, signer workflow callisto-release.yml). One of: require = a failed
      verification or missing gh aborts the step and the asset is never run; fallback (default) =
      on failure or missing gh, warn, delete the asset and install from crates.io instead (never
      run the unverified asset); skip = do not verify, warn, and use the asset. Releases built
      before the first attested release carry no attestation, hence the fallback default.
    required: false
    default: 'fallback'

runs:
  using: 'composite'
  steps:
    - name: Install Rust Toolchain & Cache
      # orin-dx/actions/setup-rust v1.1
      uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db
      with:
        components: clippy,rustfmt
        shared-key: "callisto-workspace-shared"
        save-if: "true"
      env:
        CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
        CARGO_REGISTRY_SPARSE: "true"

    - name: Install moon and the .prototools toolchain
      # moonrepo/setup-toolchain v0
      uses: moonrepo/setup-toolchain@261c62cb5b0f580c7be7c8cd0f023a2e96756095
      with:
        auto-install: true

    - name: Install or Build Callisto Binary
      shell: bash
      env:
        INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE: ${{ inputs.source }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
        INPUT_CALLISTO_VERIFICATION: ${{ inputs.verification }}
        GITHUB_ACTION_REF: ${{ github.action_ref }}
        GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
      run: bash "$GITHUB_ACTION_PATH/scripts/install-callisto.sh" # zizmor: ignore[github-env] the PATH entry is a fixed child of the trusted runner temporary directory, not action input or downloaded archive content.

     3	# callisto-action's own environment setup can call it directly by path

     5	# duplicating this logic.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	
     8	# Install into $RUNNER_TEMP so the binary never lands inside the workspace
     9	# tree (preventing accidental git-staging by downstream steps that run
    10	# "git add -A").
    11	CALLISTO_BIN_DIR="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-bin"
    12	mkdir -p "$CALLISTO_BIN_DIR"
    13	TAG_NAME="$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"
    14	SOURCE="$INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE"
    15	
    16	if [[ "$SOURCE" != "auto" && "$SOURCE" != "local" ]]; then
    17	  echo "::error::unsupported setup-callisto source '$SOURCE' (expected auto or local)"
    18	  exit 1
    19	fi
    20	
    21	# With no explicit version override, install the release this action's own
    22	# invocation is pinned to (GITHUB_ACTION_REF, github.action_ref) rather than
    23	# whatever is newest, so `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` always
    24	# installs X.Y.Z. Falls back to true "latest" when the ref is unset (local or
    25	# unpinned invocation) or matches no published callisto@ tag.
    26	if [[ "$TAG_NAME" == "latest" && -n "${GITHUB_ACTION_REF:-}" ]]; then
    27	  resolved_tag=$(git ls-remote --tags https://github.com/orin-dx/callisto.git 'callisto@*' 2>/dev/null \
    28	    | awk -v ref="$GITHUB_ACTION_REF" '$1 == ref { print $2 }' \
    29	    | sed -e 's#^refs/tags/##' -e 's/\^{}$//' \
    30	    | sort -V | tail -n1) || true

    35	fi
    36	
    37	# Validate verification mode

    65	else

# Rust Hazard Reference

Patterns are leads, not findings. Confirm a reachable bad outcome in live code and record evidence that rules out the plausible exception. Use `shared/references/hazards/rust-boundaries.md` for boundary taxonomies T7 and T10.

## T8 · False-success mutation

- Signal: a write-like function returns `Ok(())` before the required mutation or acknowledgment occurs.
- Search: write/update/set/publish functions and early `Ok` returns.
- Confirm: the caller cannot distinguish required work from a no-op and proceeds with incorrect state.

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Build one declared Callisto product artifact. This script deliberately owns
     3	# only platform compilation and archive layout; Callisto owns all release
     4	# planning, artifact identity, provenance verification, and publication.
     5	set -euo pipefail
     6	
     7	: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND:?must name cli or cross}"
     8	: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET:?must name a supported Rust target}"
     9	: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET:?must name the expected release asset}"
    10	: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT:?must name the checked-out source root}"
    11	: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR:?must name an output directory}"
    12	
    13	kind="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND"
    14	target="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET"
    15	asset="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET"
    16	source_root="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT"
    17	artifact_dir="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR"
    18	
    19	case "$kind:$target:$asset" in
    20	  cli:aarch64-apple-darwin:callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz | \
    21	  cli:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | \
    22	  cross:x86_64-unknown-linux-musl:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz)
    23	    ;;
    24	  *)
    25	    printf 'unsupported Callisto release artifact: kind=%s target=%s asset=%s\n' \
    26	      "$kind" "$target" "$asset" >&2
    27	    exit 1
    28	    ;;
    29	esac
    30	
    31	mkdir -p "$artifact_dir"
    32	
    33	case "$kind" in
    34	  cli)
    35	    rustup target add "$target"
    36	    (cd "$source_root" && cargo build --locked --release -p callisto-cli --target "$target")
    37	    tar -C "$source_root/target/$target/release" -czf "$artifact_dir/$asset" callisto
    38	    ;;
    39	  cross)
    40	    rustup target add "$target"
    41	    cargo install cross --locked --version 0.2.5
    42	    (cd "$source_root" && cross build --locked --release -p callisto-cli --target "$target")
    43	    tar -C "$source_root/target/$target/release" -czf "$artifact_dir/$asset" callisto
    44	    ;;
    45	esac

Patterns are leads, not findings. Confirm a reachable bad outcome in live code and record evidence that rules out the plausible exception. Use `shared/references/hazards/rust-boundaries.md` for boundary taxonomies T7 and T10.

## T8 · False-success mutation

- Signal: a write-like function returns `Ok(())` before the required mutation or acknowledgment occurs.
- Search: write/update/set/publish functions and early `Ok` returns.
- Confirm: the caller cannot distinguish required work from a no-op and proceeds with incorrect state.
- Refute: idempotent success is part of the contract or the caller verifies the resulting state.

## T1 · Discarded input

- Signal: a meaningful public or trait parameter is renamed with `_`, dropped, or never reaches the behavior it configures.
- Confirm: a caller supplies a value whose omission changes the outcome.
- Refute: the signature is imposed by a trait or compatibility boundary and the value is intentionally irrelevant.

## T2 · Silent fallback

- Signal: `unwrap_or*` substitutes a default after parsing, lookup, or I/O failure.
- Confirm: the default hides a state the caller must distinguish.
- Refute: the default is the documented domain value and preserves required behavior.

## T3 · Recoverable panic

- Signal: `unwrap`, `expect`, or `panic!` is reachable in reusable code.
- Confirm: valid external input or a recoverable dependency failure reaches it.
- Refute: the path is an established invariant, test-only code, or process entrypoint policy.

## T4 · Lost error

- Signal: a `Result` is assigned to `_`, dropped, or replaced by success.
- Confirm: failure changes subsequent correctness and no owner observes it.
- Refute: best-effort behavior is explicit and the discarded failure has no required consequence.

## T5 · Arithmetic overflow

- Signal: user- or data-controlled integers participate in unchecked arithmetic near a bound.
- Confirm: a reachable value overflows under the relevant build profile.
- Refute: types, validation, or domain limits prove the operation safe.

## T6 · Unsafe contract gap

- Signal: an `unsafe` block lacks a locally checkable safety contract or relies on an unverified caller invariant.
- Confirm: a reachable input violates the invariant and can cause undefined behavior.
- Refute: the contract is enforced at the boundary and covers every operation in the block.

## T9 · Incomplete or ambiguous variants

- Signal: enum conversion uses a catch-all that rejects a valid variant, or diagnostic identifiers collide where consumers require uniqueness.
- Confirm: a current variant is mishandled or a consumer cannot distinguish outcomes.
- Refute: the source is intentionally open, the fallback is contractual, or duplicate identifiers are documented aliases.

Search broadly enough to find candidates, then cite the exact caller, input, state transition, and failure for every confirmed result.
# Rust Boundary Hazards · T7 and T10

Use this reference when tracing captured intent or error information across Rust boundaries. Record each hop; matching syntax alone cannot prove loss.

## T7 · Intent lost before execution

- Signal: a plan, config, request, or options value captures a meaningful field, but a narrower downstream signature or command omits it.
- Outcome: user intent is replaced by a default or never affects the side effect.
- Evidence: identify the construction site, field value, call chain, final execution boundary, and the first hop where the value disappears.
- Refute: the field is read by an equivalent owner, intentionally ignored under a documented mode, or cannot change the selected operation.

Candidate search:

- Start from user-controlled fields and domain state, not a fixed list of names.
- Compare constructed fields with downstream parameters, command arguments, serialized payloads, and storage writes.
- Treat an unused field as confirmable only when a reachable caller supplies a value that should change behavior.

## T10 · Error context lost across a boundary

- Signal: `map_err`, string conversion, or a replacement error discards the source, diagnostic identity, span, retryability, or structured fields.
- Outcome: the caller cannot make a required decision or diagnose the underlying failure.
- Evidence: compare the source error's useful capabilities with the destination error and show which required information no longer survives.
- Refute: the destination boundary accepts only a string or stable wire shape, sensitive detail must be removed, or the lost data has no consumer.

Distinguish T10 from T4: T4 leaves a failure unowned; T10 reports a failure through a representation that may be too weak. Preserve only the context the destination reader or machine consumer needs.
# Codex Agent Roles

These are portable role instructions for Codex multi-agent work. They are resources, not a Codex TOML configuration surface: a skill reads the applicable card before it asks the host to delegate a bounded task.

The primary agent owns task decomposition, shared interfaces, final artifact assembly, verification, and all external writes. A role card defines a cognitive boundary, not a substitute owner.

| Role | Use for | Recommended tier |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `recon` | File, API, and evidence inventory | `gpt-5.6-luna` / low |
| `tracer` | Control-flow, data-flow, and boundary tracing | `gpt-5.6-terra` / medium |
| `research` | Bounded internal or external evidence collection | `gpt-5.6-terra` / medium |
| `author` | A defined draft with fixed inputs and output schema | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `implementer` | An isolated implementation batch with fixed interfaces | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `adversary` | Independent refutation or counterexample search | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `reviewer` | Evidence-led code or artifact review | `gpt-5.6-terra` / high |
| `judge` | Binding synthesis or exit decision | `gpt-5.6-sol` / high |

Use the recommended tier only when the host lets the primary agent choose it. If it does not, preserve the role boundary and run with the host default. If multi-agent work is unavailable, perform the same bounded passes sequentially in the primary agent.

## Delegation packet

Before requesting a teammate, provide this packet after reading the selected role card. The packet is the task boundary; the role card supplies the cognitive mode.

| Field | Required content |
| :--- | :--- |
| Role | One card from this directory and why that cognitive mode fits. |
| Objective | One bounded question or implementation batch, not a pipeline stage. |
| Inputs | Exact artifact IDs, criteria, paths, and relevant evidence. |
| Owned paths | Files the teammate may edit, or `read-only`. |
| Exclusions | Decisions, paths, interfaces, and external actions outside its authority. |
| Output | Required artifact or report shape, including schema when one exists. |
| Evidence | Commands, source locations, test results, or citations required to support the result. |
| Reporting | State material concerns, evidence, consequence, and confidence directly; do not soften blockers, manufacture praise, or overclaim certainty. |
| Completion | The condition that returns control to the primary agent. |

Keep synthesis, cross-batch interface decisions, final verification, commits, publication, and other external writes with the primary agent. Do not delegate coupled work merely because agent teams are available. If the packet cannot make ownership and completion unambiguous, complete the work sequentially instead.
# Tracer

Use for evidence-backed control-flow, data-flow, or boundary tracing. Start from a concrete entry point, follow each transformation and error path, and record the exact symbols and files that preserve, discard, or reinterpret the relevant state.

Return the trace, unproven edges, and the smallest reproducible scenario that exercises the path. Do not declare a defect, design a repair, or generalize from an untraced sibling path.

Use to independently try to falsify a draft, implementation claim, reachability claim, or verification result. Seek counterexamples, omitted states, boundary crossings, invalid assumptions, and missing negative tests.

Return only evidence-backed findings with exact locations and a concrete failing scenario when applicable. Do not rewrite the artifact, convert suspicion into a defect without evidence, or issue the final decision.

     8	: "${CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET:?must name a supported Rust target}"

    13	kind="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND"
    14	target="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET"
    15	asset="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET"
    16	source_root="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT"
    17	artifact_dir="$CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR"

    19	case "$kind:$target:$asset" in

    21	  cli:x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu:callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | \

needs: release-candidate
    # always(): release-candidate's own ancestors include a gate that is skipped
    # by design, and a skipped ancestor silently skips any job without a status function.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.release-candidate.result == 'success' &&
      needs.release-candidate.outputs.is_release_pr == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 20
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      has_artifacts: ${{ steps.slots.outputs.has_artifacts }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The coordinator must be the current workflow revision. Recovery
          # never rebuilds its release engine from historic source.
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Derive and hash intent
        env:
          RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          mkdir -p "$handoff_dir"
          callisto release plan --source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" \
            --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA" --artifact-repository "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" \
            --from-release-commit "$RELEASE_SOURCE_SHA" \
            --decision "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source/.callisto/release-decision.json" \
            --out "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          # Relative name: the consumers verify from a different runner OS and RUNNER_TEMP.
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 release-intent.json > release-intent.json.sha256)
      - name: Read declared artifact slot count
        id: slots
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # Own statement: set -e cannot see a substitution failing inside an echo argument.
          has_artifacts=$(jq '.artifactSlots | length > 0' "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json")
          case "$has_artifacts" in
            true|false) ;;
            *) echo "::error::artifact slot probe returned '$has_artifacts'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          echo "has_artifacts=$has_artifacts" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

    name: Build ${{ matrix.target }} from the intent-bound source tree
    needs: [plan, release-candidate]
    if: always() && needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 45
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: macos-arm64
            runner: macos-14
            target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            asset: callisto-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-gnu
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz
            kind: cli
          - id: linux-musl
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: x86_64-unknown-linux-musl
            asset: callisto-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz
            kind: cross
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: write
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
          path: release-source
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - name: Verify handoff
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          handoff_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          (cd "$handoff_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          callisto release inspect --input "$handoff_dir/release-intent.json"
          mkdir -p "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts"
      - name: Build declared artifact
        env:
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_KIND: ${{ matrix.kind }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_ASSET: ${{ matrix.asset }}
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_SOURCE_ROOT: ${{ github.workspace }}/release-source
          CALLISTO_RELEASE_ARTIFACT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
        run: |
          bash .github/scripts/build-release-artifact.sh
      - name: Attest exact artifact bytes
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2

        with:
          name: release-build-${{ matrix.id }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts/${{ matrix.asset }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          # 1 day was too short: a stuck run needing "execute" re-run days
          # later (e.g. while a workflow bug gets diagnosed and fixed) loses
          # this artifact before the fix even lands, forcing a full rerun
          # instead of just the failed job.
          retention-days: 7

    name: Assemble attested product artifacts
    needs: [build-artifact, release-candidate, plan]
    if: always() && needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true' && needs.build-artifact.result == 'success'
    timeout-minutes: 15
    outputs:
      orchestration_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
      release_source_sha: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-macos-arm64
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-linux-gnu
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build-linux-musl
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
      - name: Create exact artifact manifest
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          callisto release artifact-manifest --intent "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent/release-intent.json" --artifact-dir "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts" --out "${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-artifacts/manifest.json"
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: |
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
            ${{ runner.temp }}/release-artifacts
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

  execute:
    name: Execute approved release
    needs: [plan, build, release-candidate]
    # Artifact-less sources skip build; a failed or cancelled build must still block.
    # !cancelled() not always(): a status function still defeats the skipped-ancestor
    # rule, but cancelling the run must stop the one irreversible job.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.plan.result == 'success' &&
      (needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'false' || needs.build.result == 'success')

    concurrency:
      group: release-execute
      cancel-in-progress: false
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: $/.github/actions/setup-callisto
        with:
          source: local
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.release_source_sha }}

      # setup-callisto's own binary install): callisto release execute

      # worktree with no tracked or untracked files -- landing these inside
      # the checkout would dirty it and fail that check before anything
      # gets published.
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-intent
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-intent
      - if: needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts == 'true'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c # v8.0.1
        with:
          name: release-build
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/release-build
      - name: Verify same-run handoff before credentials
        env:
          HAS_ARTIFACTS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.has_artifacts }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          (cd "$intent_dir" && shasum -a 256 -c release-intent.json.sha256)
          if [[ "$HAS_ARTIFACTS" == true ]]; then
            cmp "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" "$build_dir/release-intent/release-intent.json"
          fi
      - name: Execute verified release
        env:
          CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          ORCHESTRATION_SHA: ${{ needs.release-candidate.outputs.orchestration_sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          intent_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-intent"
          build_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/release-build"
          receipt_dir="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          mkdir -p "$receipt_dir"
          args=(--source-root "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE/release-source" --intent "$intent_dir/release-intent.json" --receipt "$receipt_dir/release-receipt.json" --orchestration-revision "$ORCHESTRATION_SHA")
          if [[ -f "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" ]]; then
            args+=(--artifact-manifest "$build_dir/release-artifacts/manifest.json" --artifact-dir "$build_dir/release-artifacts")
          fi
          callisto release execute "${args[@]}"
      - name: Summarize receipt
        if: always()
        run: |
          receipt="${RUNNER_TEMP}/callisto-release-receipt/${GITHUB_RUN_ID}/release-receipt.json"
          if [[ -f "$receipt" ]]; then
            {
              echo '### Release receipt'
              echo '```json'
              cat "$receipt"
              echo '```'
            } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi
      - name: Upload receipt
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          # Per attempt: keeps each attempt's receipt instead of shadowing the prior one.
          name: release-receipt-attempt-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/callisto-release-receipt/${{ github.run_id }}
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 7

1	//! Pure argv construction for "publish a package to its registry", plus
     2	//! subprocess-output classification for the same three ecosystems (Cargo,
     3	//! npm, PyPI).
     4	//!
     5	//! This module owns exactly two questions per ecosystem: *what command do we
     6	//! run* (given package/plan facts and already-detected environment facts --
     7	//! never a [`callisto_model::CommandRunner`] call of its own) and *what did
     8	//! the finished command's output mean*. Actually invoking the command, and
     9	//! any retry/backoff policy around a failed attempt, is the caller's job --
    10	//! see the durable release executor's single production publish path.
    11	//!
    12	//! A small amount of local filesystem reading happens here (the Cargo
    13	//! on-disk version check, npm package-manager detection from lockfiles, the
    14	//! PyPI interpreter's PATH lookup) -- that's "gathering the facts needed to
    15	//! build the right argv", not executing a publish. It never shells out.
    16	
    17	use std::ffi::OsStr;
    18	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    19	use std::time::Duration;
    20	
    21	use callisto_manifests::WorkspaceCargoResolver;
    22	use callisto_model::{
    23	    normalize_pypi_package_name, CommandOutput, Ecosystem, NpmAccess, PackageId, PublishOutcome, RegistryError, Version,
    24	};
    25	
    26	use crate::error::{GraphError, ReleasePreconditionRequirement};
    27	
    28	/// Default fallback wait (seconds) when a registry does not supply a
    29	/// `retry_after` value and the classifier cannot parse one from output.
    30	const DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 60;
    31	
    32	/// One subprocess invocation: program, args, and working directory. Building
    33	/// this is the entire job of the `*_publish_argv` functions below --
    34	/// executing it is the caller's.
    35	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    36	pub struct Argv {
    37	    pub program: String,
    38	    pub args: Vec<String>,
    39	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
    40	}
    41	
    42	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- cargo
    43	
    44	/// Builds the exact `cargo publish` argv for one crate: `--manifest-path`
    45	/// (so the caller can keep the workspace root as its own working directory)
    46	/// plus `--locked`, so a stale `Cargo.lock` fails the publish immediately
    47	/// instead of `cargo` silently re-resolving one at publish time.
    48	/// `registry_key` is `Some` only for a non-default registry -- crates.io is
    49	/// the implicit default and never needs `--registry`.
    50	///
    51	/// Before returning, verifies that the on-disk `Cargo.toml` version under
    52	/// `package_dir` (resolving `version.workspace = true` against the
    53	/// workspace root's `[workspace.package].version` when present) matches
    54	/// `version` -- this is the one behavior `SubprocessRegistryClient` had that
    55	/// the durable release executor's own `dispatch_registry` had silently
    56	/// dropped: it catches the common mistake of running `release execute`
    57	/// without first running `callisto version`, which would otherwise silently
    58	/// publish the old on-disk version.
    59	pub fn cargo_publish_argv(
    60	    workspace_root: &Path,
    61	    package_dir: &Path,
    62	    package_name: &str,
    63	    version: &Version,
    64	    registry_key: Option<&str>,
    65	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
    66	    verify_cargo_ondisk_version(workspace_root, package_dir, package_name, version)?;
    67	
    68	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    69	    let mut args = vec![
    70	        "publish".to_string(),
    71	        "--manifest-path".to_string(),
    72	        manifest_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
    73	        "--locked".to_string(),
    74	    ];
    75	    if let Some(reg) = registry_key {
    76	        args.push("--registry".to_string());
    77	        args.push(reg.to_string());
    78	    }
    79	    Ok(Argv {
    80	        program: "cargo".to_string(),
    81	        args,
    82	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
    83	    })
    84	}
    85	
    86	fn verify_cargo_ondisk_version(
    87	    workspace_root: &Path,
    88	    package_dir: &Path,
    89	    package_name: &str,
    90	    planned: &Version,
    91	) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
    92	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    93	    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
    94	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
    95	        message: error.to_string(),
    96	    })?;
    97	    // Parse only the [package].version field -- no need for full CST. A
    98	    // permissive `toml::Value` intermediate rather than a direct `String`
    99	    // deserialization, because `version.workspace = true` (Cargo's
   100	    // workspace-version-inheritance syntax) parses `version` as a table, not
   101	    // a string.
   102	    let parsed = toml::from_str::<toml::Value>(&contents).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   103	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
   104	        message: error.to_string(),
   105	    })?;
   106	    let version_value =
   107	        parsed
   108	            .get("package")
   109	            .and_then(|p| p.get("version"))
   110	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   111	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
   112	                message: "missing [package].version".to_string(),
   113	            })?;
   114	
   115	    let on_disk = if let Some(s) = version_value.as_str() {
   116	        s.to_string()
   117	    } else if version_value.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
   118	        let root_manifest_path = workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml");
   119	        let resolver = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_manifest_path)?;
   120	        let ws_version = resolver
   121	            .workspace_version()?
   122	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   123	                path: root_manifest_path.clone(),
   124	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but the workspace root has no [workspace.package].version"
   125	                    .to_string(),
   126	            })?;
   127	        ws_version.render().to_string()
   128	    } else {
   129	        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   130	            path: manifest_path,
   131	            message: "[package].version is neither a string nor a `{ workspace = true }` table".to_string(),
   132	        });
   133	    };
   134	
   135	    let found = Version::parse(&on_disk, planned.grammar())?;
   136	    if found != *planned {
   137	        return Err(GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift {
   138	            package: PackageId::Prefixed {
   139	                ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo,
   140	                name: package_name.to_string(),
   141	            },
   142	            expected: planned.clone(),
   143	            found,
   144	        });
   145	    }
   146	    Ok(())
   147	}

   151	/// The npm-compatible package manager a workspace uses, detected from
   152	/// lockfile presence. Each one needs a materially different invocation to
   153	/// publish a single named package out of a monorepo -- see
   154	/// [`npm_publish_argv`].
   155	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   156	pub enum NpmPackageManager {
   157	    Pnpm,
   158	    Yarn,
   159	    Bun,
   160	    Npm,
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Detects the npm-compatible package manager for `workspace_root` from
   164	/// lockfile presence. Detection priority: pnpm > yarn > bun > npm (default).
   165	///
   166	/// This is real, live-today correctness content: the durable release
   167	/// executor's `dispatch_registry` used to hardcode plain `npm publish`
   168	/// regardless of which package manager a workspace actually uses, so a pnpm
   169	/// or yarn workspace published with the wrong tool.
   170	pub fn detect_npm_package_manager(workspace_root: &Path) -> NpmPackageManager {
   171	    if workspace_root.join("pnpm-lock.yaml").exists() {
   172	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm
   173	    } else if workspace_root.join("yarn.lock").exists() {
   174	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn
   175	    } else if workspace_root.join("bun.lockb").exists() || workspace_root.join("bun.lock").exists() {
   176	        // bun.lockb is the legacy binary lockfile format; bun.lock (text) is
   177	        // written by Bun >= 1.1.1. Both signal a bun-managed workspace.
   178	        NpmPackageManager::Bun
   179	    } else {
   180	        NpmPackageManager::Npm
   181	    }
   182	}

   184	/// Builds the npm-ecosystem publish argv for one package, given the
   185	/// already-detected `package_manager` (see [`detect_npm_package_manager`]).
   186	///
   187	/// | Package manager | Program | Base args                                  |
   188	/// |------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
   189	/// | Pnpm             | `pnpm`  | `publish --filter=<name> --no-git-checks`  |
   190	/// | Yarn             | `yarn`  | `workspace <name> npm publish`             |
   191	/// | Bun              | `bun`   | `publish` (run from `package_dir`)         |
   192	/// | Npm              | `npm`   | `publish --workspace=<name>`               |
   193	///
   194	/// `--filter=`/`--workspace=` use the joined form so the name cannot be
   195	/// re-read as an option. Yarn takes the name positionally and has no joined
   196	/// spelling, so there it rests on `ReleasePackageId`'s leading-`-` rejection.
   197	///
   198	/// `tag`/`access`/`registry` are appended to every variant's base args.
   199	/// `package_dir` is only used for bun: it has no `--filter`/`--workspace`
   200	/// flag to target one package by name, so it alone must run from the
   201	/// package's own directory rather than the workspace root.
   202	pub fn npm_publish_argv(
   203	    workspace_root: &Path,
   204	    package_dir: &Path,
   205	    package_name: &str,
   206	    package_manager: NpmPackageManager,
   207	    tag: Option<&str>,
   208	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   209	    registry: Option<&str>,
   210	) -> Argv {
   211	    let extra = npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry);
   212	
   213	    let (program, mut args, cwd) = match package_manager {
   214	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm => (
   215	            "pnpm",
   216	            vec![
   217	                "publish".to_string(),
   218	                // `--filter=<name>`, not `--filter <name>`: the joined form
   219	                // cannot be re-read as an option even if a name slipped past
   220	                // `ReleasePackageId`'s charset rule.
   221	                format!("--filter={package_name}"),
   222	                // pnpm >= 7 refuses to publish from a dirty working tree by
   223	                // default. After `callisto version` stages manifest bumps,
   224	                // the tree is always dirty until the operator commits, so
   225	                // this bypasses the git-status check.
   226	                "--no-git-checks".to_string(),
   227	            ],
   228	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   229	        ),
   230	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn => (
   231	            "yarn",
   232	            vec![
   233	                "workspace".to_string(),
   234	                package_name.to_string(),
   235	                "npm".to_string(),
   236	                "publish".to_string(),
   237	            ],
   238	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   239	        ),
   240	        NpmPackageManager::Bun => ("bun", vec!["publish".to_string()], workspace_root.join(package_dir)),
   241	        NpmPackageManager::Npm => (
   242	            "npm",
   243	            vec!["publish".to_string(), format!("--workspace={package_name}")],
   244	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   245	        ),
   246	    };
   247	    args.extend(extra);
   248	    Argv {
   249	        program: program.to_string(),
   250	        args,
   251	        cwd,
   252	    }
   253	}

   255	/// The access an npm package publishes with: the explicit `publishConfig.access`,
   256	/// else `public` for a scoped `@scope/name` (npm defaults scoped packages to restricted).
   257	pub fn npm_default_access(name: &str, explicit: Option<NpmAccess>) -> Option<NpmAccess> {
   258	    explicit.or_else(|| name.starts_with('@').then_some(NpmAccess::Public))
   259	}
   260	
   261	/// `--tag`/`--access`/`--registry`, shared by every npm-ecosystem publish argv.
   262	fn npm_publish_flags(
   263	    package_name: &str,
   264	    tag: Option<&str>,
   265	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   266	    registry: Option<&str>,
   267	) -> Vec<String> {
   268	    let mut extra: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   269	    if let Some(t) = tag {
   270	        extra.push("--tag".to_string());
   271	        extra.push(t.to_string());
   272	    }
   273	    if let Some(access) = npm_default_access(package_name, access) {
   274	        extra.push("--access".to_string());
   275	        extra.push(
   276	            match access {
   277	                NpmAccess::Public => "public",
   278	                NpmAccess::Restricted => "restricted",
   279	            }
   280	            .to_string(),
   281	        );
   282	    }
   283	    if let Some(reg) = registry {
   284	        extra.push("--registry".to_string());
   285	        extra.push(reg.to_string());
   286	    }
   287	    extra
   288	}

   290	/// Publishes the package in `package_dir` by path: `npm publish <dir>` from the
   291	/// workspace root, whatever the package manager. pnpm `--filter`, yarn
   292	/// `workspace`, and npm `--workspace` select only workspace members, and an npm
   293	/// platform package directory usually is not one. The path is absolute, so it
   294	/// cannot be read as an option.
   295	pub fn npm_publish_directory_argv(
   296	    workspace_root: &Path,
   297	    package_dir: &Path,
   298	    package_name: &str,
   299	    tag: Option<&str>,
   300	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   301	    registry: Option<&str>,
   302	) -> Argv {
   303	    let mut args = vec![
   304	        "publish".to_string(),
   305	        workspace_root.join(package_dir).to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
   306	    ];
   307	    args.extend(npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry));
   308	    Argv {
   309	        program: "npm".to_string(),
   310	        args,
   311	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   312	    }
   313	}

   316	
   317	/// The public warehouses twine (>= 5) allows `--skip-existing` against.
   318	/// Matches twine's own `repository.WAREHOUSE`/`repository.TEST_WAREHOUSE`
   319	/// constants exactly, including the `upload.` subdomain -- PyPI's upload
   320	/// endpoint, not its browsing/simple-index host (`pypi.org`).
   321	const PYPI_WAREHOUSE_URL: &str = "https://upload.pypi.org/";
   322	const PYPI_TEST_WAREHOUSE_URL: &str = "https://test.pypi.org/";
   323	
   324	/// Whether twine accepts `--skip-existing` for this upload target. Twine's
   325	/// own `verify_feature_capability` (added in twine 5) raises
   326	/// `UnsupportedConfiguration` and refuses to run at all when `--skip-existing`
   327	/// is set against any repository URL other than the public warehouses --
   328	/// confirmed live against a real local `pypiserver`: the upload never reaches
   329	/// the wire. `index: None` means twine's own default target (`.pypirc`'s
   330	/// `pypi` alias, `https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/`), which is always safe.
   331	fn twine_accepts_skip_existing(index: Option<&str>) -> bool {
   332	    match index {
   333	        None => true,
   334	        Some(url) => url.starts_with(PYPI_WAREHOUSE_URL) || url.starts_with(PYPI_TEST_WAREHOUSE_URL),
   335	    }
   336	}

   338	/// Builds the two-step PyPI publish argv sequence: build the sdist and
   339	/// wheel into `dist/`, then upload the exact `dist/<normalized-name>-
   340	/// <version>*` glob via `twine upload`. Both steps run from `package_dir` so
   341	/// `dist/` resolves to that package's own directory in a monorepo, and
   342	/// neither ever builds into or uploads from a fresh temporary directory --
   343	/// `twine`'s own glob targets exactly the artifacts this `python -m build`
   344	/// invocation just produced, not whatever else happens to be sitting in
   345	/// `dist/`.
   346	///
   347	/// `--skip-existing` is included only when `twine_accepts_skip_existing`
   348	/// allows it for `index`; it's mostly redundant for the durable release path
   349	/// anyway, since the operation is only ever dispatched after an `Absent`
   350	/// preflight observation of the exact same registry.
   351	///
   352	/// Package name is normalized to PEP 427 wheel-filename form (lowercased,
   353	/// `-`/`.` -> `_`) before building the glob; `twine` expands the glob
   354	/// internally, so the literal `*` is safe with no shell involved.
   355	/// `index: Some` inserts `--repository-url <url>` before the glob, to target
   356	/// a private index (Nexus/Artifactory PyPI proxy, or a local test registry)
   357	/// instead of public PyPI.
   358	///
   359	/// The build step's interpreter comes from `resolve_python_interpreter` --
   360	/// `python3` first, `python` as a fallback -- rather than a hardcoded
   361	/// `python`, since many systems (macOS, Debian) ship no bare `python`.
   362	pub fn pypi_publish_argv(
   363	    workspace_root: &Path,
   364	    package_dir: &Path,
   365	    package_name: &str,
   366	    version: &Version,
   367	    index: Option<&str>,
   368	) -> Result<Vec<Argv>, GraphError> {
   369	    let interpreter = resolve_python_interpreter(std::env::var_os("PATH").as_deref())?;
   370	    let cwd = workspace_root.join(package_dir);
   371	    let build = Argv {
   372	        program: interpreter.to_string(),
   373	        args: vec![
   374	            "-m".to_string(),
   375	            "build".to_string(),
   376	            "--sdist".to_string(),
   377	            "--wheel".to_string(),
   378	            "--outdir".to_string(),
   379	            "dist/".to_string(),
   380	        ],
   381	        cwd: cwd.clone(),
   382	    };
   383	
   384	    let normalized = normalize_pypi_package_name(package_name);
   385	    let pattern = format!("dist/{normalized}-{}*", version.render());
   386	    let mut upload_args = vec!["upload".to_string()];
   387	    if twine_accepts_skip_existing(index) {
   388	        upload_args.push("--skip-existing".to_string());
   389	    }
   390	    if let Some(idx) = index {
   391	        upload_args.push("--repository-url".to_string());
   392	        upload_args.push(idx.to_string());
   393	    }
   394	    upload_args.push(pattern);
   395	    let upload = Argv {
   396	        program: "twine".to_string(),
   397	        args: upload_args,
   398	        cwd,
   399	    };
   400	
   401	    Ok(vec![build, upload])
   402	}
