   404	/// Resolves the interpreter for the PyPI build step's `python -m build`:
   405	/// prefers `python3` -- the only name macOS and Debian systems guarantee --
   406	/// and falls back to bare `python` for systems that only ship that. Errors
   407	/// naming both when neither is on `path_value`.
   408	///
   409	/// `path_value` is injected rather than read from `$PATH` directly so tests
   410	/// can exercise both resolutions and the error without mutating process-wide
   411	/// environment state.
   412	fn resolve_python_interpreter(path_value: Option<&OsStr>) -> Result<&'static str, GraphError> {
   413	    if exists_on_path("python3", path_value) {
   414	        Ok("python3")
   415	    } else if exists_on_path("python", path_value) {
   416	        Ok("python")
   417	    } else {
   418	        Err(GraphError::ReleasePreconditionUnmet {
   419	            requirement: ReleasePreconditionRequirement::PythonInterpreterOnPath,
   420	        })
   421	    }
   422	}
   423	
   424	/// Whether `program` exists as a file in some directory of `path_value` --
   425	/// PATH-lookup semantics, without ever spawning it.
   426	fn exists_on_path(program: &str, path_value: Option<&OsStr>) -> bool {
   427	    path_value.is_some_and(|path| std::env::split_paths(path).any(|dir| dir.join(program).is_file()))
   428	}

   431	
   432	fn combined_lower(output: &CommandOutput) -> String {
   433	    format!("{}\n{}", output.stdout, output.stderr).to_lowercase()
   434	}
   435	
   436	/// Parses a numeric retry-after value (seconds) as reported by a registry
   437	/// tool's output.
   438	fn parse_retry_after(raw: &str) -> Option<Duration> {
   439	    raw.trim().parse::<u64>().ok().map(Duration::from_secs)
   440	}
   441	
   442	/// Looks for a `retry after <N>` mention in already-lowercased text and
   443	/// parses `<N>` as a whole-second duration.
   444	fn extract_retry_after_duration(text_lower: &str) -> Option<Duration> {
   445	    const NEEDLE: &str = "retry after ";
   446	    let idx = text_lower.find(NEEDLE)?;
   447	    let rest = &text_lower[idx + NEEDLE.len()..];
   448	    let token = rest.split_whitespace().next()?;
   449	    let digits: String = token.chars().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
   450	    if digits.is_empty() {
   451	        return None;
   452	    }
   453	    parse_retry_after(&digits)
   454	}
   455	
   456	fn detect_rate_limit(text_lower: &str) -> Option<RegistryError> {
   457	    // Match rate-limit signals with context, never on bare digits alone.
   458	    // Bare "429" in cargo's compressed-size output ("429.1KiB compressed")
   459	    // would otherwise trigger this. Require at least one contextual phrase
   460	    // alongside any "429".
   461	    let is_rate_limited = text_lower.contains("too many requests")
   462	        || text_lower.contains("rate limit")
   463	        || text_lower.contains("erate_limit")
   464	        || (text_lower.contains("429")
   465	            && (text_lower.contains("too many") || text_lower.contains("rate") || text_lower.contains("retry")));
   466	    if is_rate_limited {
   467	        let dur = extract_retry_after_duration(text_lower).unwrap_or(Duration::from_secs(DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECS));
   468	        Some(RegistryError::RateLimited(dur))
   469	    } else {
   470	        None
   471	    }
   472	}
   473	
   474	fn detect_auth_failure(text_lower: &str, raw_stderr: &CommandOutput) -> Option<RegistryError> {
   475	    // Match "401"/"403" with context, never on bare digits alone -- same
   476	    // rationale as detect_rate_limit's guard against bare "429": a byte
   477	    // count or elapsed-time figure in cargo's own packaging/build output
   478	    // ("403129 bytes", "elapsed 4013ms") would otherwise misclassify an
   479	    // unrelated failure as an auth failure.
   480	    if (text_lower.contains("401") && text_lower.contains("auth"))
   481	        || (text_lower.contains("403") && (text_lower.contains("auth") || text_lower.contains("forbidden")))
   482	        || text_lower.contains("authentication")
   483	        || text_lower.contains("not logged in")
   484	        || text_lower.contains("invalid token")
   485	        || text_lower.contains("forbidden")
   486	    {
   487	        Some(RegistryError::AuthFailed(raw_stderr.redacted_stderr()))
   488	    } else {
   489	        None
   490	    }
   491	}

   493	/// Classifies combined `cargo publish` output into a [`PublishOutcome`] or
   494	/// [`RegistryError`].
   495	pub(crate) fn classify_cargo_output(output: &CommandOutput) -> Result<PublishOutcome, RegistryError> {
   496	    let combined = combined_lower(output);
   497	
   498	    if combined.contains("already exists") || combined.contains("already uploaded") {
   499	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished);
   500	    }
   501	    if output.success() {
   502	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::Published);
   503	    }
   504	    if let Some(err) = detect_rate_limit(&combined) {
   505	        return Err(err);
   506	    }
   507	    if let Some(err) = detect_auth_failure(&combined, output) {
   508	        return Err(err);
   509	    }
   510	    Err(RegistryError::Other(format!(
   511	        "cargo publish failed (exit {:?}): {}",
   512	        output.exit_code,
   513	        output.redacted_stderr().trim()
   514	    )))
   515	}

   517	/// Classifies combined `npm publish` (or `pnpm`/`yarn`/`bun` equivalent)
   518	/// output into a [`PublishOutcome`] or [`RegistryError`].
   519	pub(crate) fn classify_npm_publish_output(output: &CommandOutput) -> Result<PublishOutcome, RegistryError> {
   520	    let combined = combined_lower(output);
   521	
   522	    if combined.contains("epublishconflict")
   523	        || combined.contains("previously published")
   524	        || combined.contains("cannot publish over")
   525	        || combined.contains("e409")
   526	        || combined.contains("409 conflict")
   527	    {
   528	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished);
   529	    }
   530	    if output.success() {
   531	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::Published);
   532	    }
   533	    if let Some(err) = detect_rate_limit(&combined) {
   534	        return Err(err);
   535	    }
   536	    if let Some(err) = detect_auth_failure(&combined, output) {
   537	        return Err(err);
   538	    }
   539	    Err(RegistryError::Other(format!(
   540	        "npm publish failed (exit {:?}): {}",
   541	        output.exit_code,
   542	        output.redacted_stderr().trim()
   543	    )))
   544	}
   545	
   546	/// Classifies combined `twine upload` output into a [`PublishOutcome`] or
   547	/// [`RegistryError`].
   548	///
   549	/// Priority order (highest wins):
   550	/// 1. `"already exist"` (from `--skip-existing`) without `"uploading"` ->
   551	///    [`PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished`] (all artifacts skipped). Both
   552	///    phrases present means at least one artifact was freshly uploaded ->
   553	///    `Published`. Handles `dist/` accumulating stale pre-release
   554	///    artifacts: `dist/my_pkg-1.0.0*` matches both `my_pkg-1.0.0a0.whl`
   555	///    (skipped) and `my_pkg-1.0.0.whl` (uploaded), producing mixed output.
   556	///    Only reachable when [`pypi_publish_argv`] included `--skip-existing`
   557	///    (a public-warehouse target); a private-index conflict never emits this
   558	///    text (confirmed live against `pypiserver`: a real conflict there is a
   559	///    bare `409 Conflict`), so it falls through to `RegistryError::Other`
   560	///    below instead -- an intentional fail-closed outcome. The durable
   561	///    release executor only ever calls this after an `Absent` preflight
   562	///    observation of the very same registry, so a private-index conflict
   563	///    here is a rare race, not the common path; a rerun converges through
   564	///    that same observation rather than through this classifier guessing at
   565	///    conflict text with no stable, portable shape across index servers.
   566	/// 2. Zero exit code with no skip-only mention -> [`PublishOutcome::Published`].
   567	/// 3. Rate-limit signal (`429`, `too many requests`, `rate limit`) ->
   568	///    [`RegistryError::RateLimited`] with a parsed or default 60-second
   569	///    retry-after duration.
   570	/// 4. Auth-failure signal (`401`, `403`, `authentication`, etc.) ->
   571	///    [`RegistryError::AuthFailed`].
   572	/// 5. Anything else -> [`RegistryError::Other`].
   573	pub(crate) fn classify_twine_output(output: &CommandOutput) -> Result<PublishOutcome, RegistryError> {
   574	    let combined = combined_lower(output);
   575	
   576	    let has_skip = combined.contains("already exist");
   577	    let has_upload = combined.contains("uploading");
   578	    if has_skip && !has_upload {
   579	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished);
   580	    }
   581	    if output.success() {
   582	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::Published);
   583	    }
   584	    if let Some(err) = detect_rate_limit(&combined) {
   585	        return Err(err);
   586	    }
   587	    if let Some(err) = detect_auth_failure(&combined, output) {
   588	        return Err(err);
   589	    }
   590	    Err(RegistryError::Other(format!(
   591	        "twine upload failed (exit {:?}): {}",
   592	        output.exit_code,
   593	        output.redacted_stderr().trim()
   594	    )))
   595	}

1	//! Pure argv construction for "publish a package to its registry", plus
     2	//! subprocess-output classification for the same three ecosystems (Cargo,
     3	//! npm, PyPI).
     4	//!
     5	//! This module owns exactly two questions per ecosystem: *what command do we
     6	//! run* (given package/plan facts and already-detected environment facts --
     7	//! never a [`callisto_model::CommandRunner`] call of its own) and *what did
     8	//! the finished command's output mean*. Actually invoking the command, and
     9	//! any retry/backoff policy around a failed attempt, is the caller's job --
    10	//! see the durable release executor's single production publish path.
    11	//!
    12	//! A small amount of local filesystem reading happens here (the Cargo
    13	//! on-disk version check, npm package-manager detection from lockfiles, the
    14	//! PyPI interpreter's PATH lookup) -- that's "gathering the facts needed to
    15	//! build the right argv", not executing a publish. It never shells out.
    16	
    17	use std::ffi::OsStr;
    18	use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    19	use std::time::Duration;
    20	
    21	use callisto_manifests::WorkspaceCargoResolver;
    22	use callisto_model::{
    23	    normalize_pypi_package_name, CommandOutput, Ecosystem, NpmAccess, PackageId, PublishOutcome, RegistryError, Version,
    24	};
    25	
    26	use crate::error::{GraphError, ReleasePreconditionRequirement};
    27	
    28	/// Default fallback wait (seconds) when a registry does not supply a
    29	/// `retry_after` value and the classifier cannot parse one from output.
    30	const DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECS: u64 = 60;
    31	
    32	/// One subprocess invocation: program, args, and working directory. Building
    33	/// this is the entire job of the `*_publish_argv` functions below --
    34	/// executing it is the caller's.
    35	#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
    36	pub struct Argv {
    37	    pub program: String,
    38	    pub args: Vec<String>,
    39	    pub cwd: PathBuf,
    40	}
    41	
    42	// ---------------------------------------------------------------- cargo
    43	
    44	/// Builds the exact `cargo publish` argv for one crate: `--manifest-path`
    45	/// (so the caller can keep the workspace root as its own working directory)
    46	/// plus `--locked`, so a stale `Cargo.lock` fails the publish immediately
    47	/// instead of `cargo` silently re-resolving one at publish time.
    48	/// `registry_key` is `Some` only for a non-default registry -- crates.io is
    49	/// the implicit default and never needs `--registry`.
    50	///
    51	/// Before returning, verifies that the on-disk `Cargo.toml` version under
    52	/// `package_dir` (resolving `version.workspace = true` against the
    53	/// workspace root's `[workspace.package].version` when present) matches
    54	/// `version` -- this is the one behavior `SubprocessRegistryClient` had that
    55	/// the durable release executor's own `dispatch_registry` had silently
    56	/// dropped: it catches the common mistake of running `release execute`
    57	/// without first running `callisto version`, which would otherwise silently
    58	/// publish the old on-disk version.
    59	pub fn cargo_publish_argv(
    60	    workspace_root: &Path,
    61	    package_dir: &Path,
    62	    package_name: &str,
    63	    version: &Version,
    64	    registry_key: Option<&str>,
    65	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
    66	    verify_cargo_ondisk_version(workspace_root, package_dir, package_name, version)?;
    67	
    68	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    69	    let mut args = vec![
    70	        "publish".to_string(),
    71	        "--manifest-path".to_string(),
    72	        manifest_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
    73	        "--locked".to_string(),
    74	    ];
    75	    if let Some(reg) = registry_key {
    76	        args.push("--registry".to_string());
    77	        args.push(reg.to_string());
    78	    }
    79	    Ok(Argv {
    80	        program: "cargo".to_string(),
    81	        args,
    82	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
    83	    })
    84	}

    86	fn verify_cargo_ondisk_version(
    87	    workspace_root: &Path,
    88	    package_dir: &Path,
    89	    package_name: &str,
    90	    planned: &Version,
    91	) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
    92	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    93	    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
    94	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
    95	        message: error.to_string(),
    96	    })?;
    97	    // Parse only the [package].version field -- no need for full CST. A
    98	    // permissive `toml::Value` intermediate rather than a direct `String`
    99	    // deserialization, because `version.workspace = true` (Cargo's
   100	    // workspace-version-inheritance syntax) parses `version` as a table, not
   101	    // a string.
   102	    let parsed = toml::from_str::<toml::Value>(&contents).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   103	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
   104	        message: error.to_string(),
   105	    })?;
   106	    let version_value =
   107	        parsed
   108	            .get("package")
   109	            .and_then(|p| p.get("version"))
   110	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   111	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
   112	                message: "missing [package].version".to_string(),
   113	            })?;
   114	
   115	    let on_disk = if let Some(s) = version_value.as_str() {
   116	        s.to_string()
   117	    } else if version_value.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
   118	        let root_manifest_path = workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml");
   119	        let resolver = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_manifest_path)?;
   120	        let ws_version = resolver
   121	            .workspace_version()?
   122	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   123	                path: root_manifest_path.clone(),
   124	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but the workspace root has no [workspace.package].version"
   125	                    .to_string(),
   126	            })?;
   127	        ws_version.render().to_string()
   128	    } else {
   129	        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   130	            path: manifest_path,
   131	            message: "[package].version is neither a string nor a `{ workspace = true }` table".to_string(),
   132	        });
   133	    };
   134	
   135	    let found = Version::parse(&on_disk, planned.grammar())?;
   136	    if found != *planned {
   137	        return Err(GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift {
   138	            package: PackageId::Prefixed {
   139	                ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo,
   140	                name: package_name.to_string(),
   141	            },
   142	            expected: planned.clone(),
   143	            found,
   144	        });
   145	    }
   146	    Ok(())
   147	}

   151	/// The npm-compatible package manager a workspace uses, detected from
   152	/// lockfile presence. Each one needs a materially different invocation to
   153	/// publish a single named package out of a monorepo -- see
   154	/// [`npm_publish_argv`].
   155	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   156	pub enum NpmPackageManager {
   157	    Pnpm,
   158	    Yarn,
   159	    Bun,
   160	    Npm,
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Detects the npm-compatible package manager for `workspace_root` from
   164	/// lockfile presence. Detection priority: pnpm > yarn > bun > npm (default).
   165	///
   166	/// This is real, live-today correctness content: the durable release
   167	/// executor's `dispatch_registry` used to hardcode plain `npm publish`
   168	/// regardless of which package manager a workspace actually uses, so a pnpm
   169	/// or yarn workspace published with the wrong tool.
   170	pub fn detect_npm_package_manager(workspace_root: &Path) -> NpmPackageManager {
   171	    if workspace_root.join("pnpm-lock.yaml").exists() {
   172	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm
   173	    } else if workspace_root.join("yarn.lock").exists() {
   174	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn
   175	    } else if workspace_root.join("bun.lockb").exists() || workspace_root.join("bun.lock").exists() {
   176	        // bun.lockb is the legacy binary lockfile format; bun.lock (text) is
   177	        // written by Bun >= 1.1.1. Both signal a bun-managed workspace.
   178	        NpmPackageManager::Bun
   179	    } else {
   180	        NpmPackageManager::Npm
   181	    }
   182	}

   184	/// Builds the npm-ecosystem publish argv for one package, given the
   185	/// already-detected `package_manager` (see [`detect_npm_package_manager`]).
   186	///
   187	/// | Package manager | Program | Base args                                  |
   188	/// |------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
   189	/// | Pnpm             | `pnpm`  | `publish --filter=<name> --no-git-checks`  |
   190	/// | Yarn             | `yarn`  | `workspace <name> npm publish`             |
   191	/// | Bun              | `bun`   | `publish` (run from `package_dir`)         |
   192	/// | Npm              | `npm`   | `publish --workspace=<name>`               |
   193	///
   194	/// `--filter=`/`--workspace=` use the joined form so the name cannot be
   195	/// re-read as an option. Yarn takes the name positionally and has no joined
   196	/// spelling, so there it rests on `ReleasePackageId`'s leading-`-` rejection.
   197	///
   198	/// `tag`/`access`/`registry` are appended to every variant's base args.
   199	/// `package_dir` is only used for bun: it has no `--filter`/`--workspace`
   200	/// flag to target one package by name, so it alone must run from the
   201	/// package's own directory rather than the workspace root.
   202	pub fn npm_publish_argv(
   203	    workspace_root: &Path,
   204	    package_dir: &Path,
   205	    package_name: &str,
   206	    package_manager: NpmPackageManager,
   207	    tag: Option<&str>,
   208	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   209	    registry: Option<&str>,
   210	) -> Argv {
   211	    let extra = npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry);
   212	
   213	    let (program, mut args, cwd) = match package_manager {
   214	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm => (
   215	            "pnpm",
   216	            vec![
   217	                "publish".to_string(),
   218	                // `--filter=<name>`, not `--filter <name>`: the joined form
   219	                // cannot be re-read as an option even if a name slipped past
   220	                // `ReleasePackageId`'s charset rule.
   221	                format!("--filter={package_name}"),
   222	                // pnpm >= 7 refuses to publish from a dirty working tree by
   223	                // default. After `callisto version` stages manifest bumps,
   224	                // the tree is always dirty until the operator commits, so
   225	                // this bypasses the git-status check.
   226	                "--no-git-checks".to_string(),
   227	            ],
   228	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   229	        ),
   230	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn => (
   231	            "yarn",
   232	            vec![
   233	                "workspace".to_string(),
   234	                package_name.to_string(),
   235	                "npm".to_string(),
   236	                "publish".to_string(),
   237	            ],
   238	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   239	        ),
   240	        NpmPackageManager::Bun => ("bun", vec!["publish".to_string()], workspace_root.join(package_dir)),
   241	        NpmPackageManager::Npm => (
   242	            "npm",
   243	            vec!["publish".to_string(), format!("--workspace={package_name}")],
   244	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   245	        ),
   246	    };
   247	    args.extend(extra);
   248	    Argv {
   249	        program: program.to_string(),
   250	        args,
   251	        cwd,
   252	    }
   253	}

   255	/// The access an npm package publishes with: the explicit `publishConfig.access`,
   256	/// else `public` for a scoped `@scope/name` (npm defaults scoped packages to restricted).
   257	pub fn npm_default_access(name: &str, explicit: Option<NpmAccess>) -> Option<NpmAccess> {
   258	    explicit.or_else(|| name.starts_with('@').then_some(NpmAccess::Public))
   259	}

   261	/// `--tag`/`--access`/`--registry`, shared by every npm-ecosystem publish argv.
   262	fn npm_publish_flags(
   263	    package_name: &str,
   264	    tag: Option<&str>,
   265	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   266	    registry: Option<&str>,
   267	) -> Vec<String> {
   268	    let mut extra: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   269	    if let Some(t) = tag {
   270	        extra.push("--tag".to_string());
   271	        extra.push(t.to_string());
   272	    }
   273	    if let Some(access) = npm_default_access(package_name, access) {
   274	        extra.push("--access".to_string());
   275	        extra.push(
   276	            match access {
   277	                NpmAccess::Public => "public",
   278	                NpmAccess::Restricted => "restricted",
   279	            }
   280	            .to_string(),
   281	        );
   282	    }
   283	    if let Some(reg) = registry {
   284	        extra.push("--registry".to_string());
   285	        extra.push(reg.to_string());
   286	    }
   287	    extra
   288	}

   290	/// Publishes the package in `package_dir` by path: `npm publish <dir>` from the
   291	/// workspace root, whatever the package manager. pnpm `--filter`, yarn
   292	/// `workspace`, and npm `--workspace` select only workspace members, and an npm
   293	/// platform package directory usually is not one. The path is absolute, so it
   294	/// cannot be read as an option.

   301	    registry: Option<&str>,

   316	
   317	/// The public warehouses twine (>= 5) allows `--skip-existing` against.
   318	/// Matches twine's own `repository.WAREHOUSE`/`repository.TEST_WAREHOUSE`
   319	/// constants exactly, including the `upload.` subdomain -- PyPI's upload
   320	/// endpoint, not its browsing/simple-index host (`pypi.org`).
   321	const PYPI_WAREHOUSE_URL: &str = "https://upload.pypi.org/";
   322	const PYPI_TEST_WAREHOUSE_URL: &str = "https://test.pypi.org/";
   323	
   324	/// Whether twine accepts `--skip-existing` for this upload target. Twine's
   325	/// own `verify_feature_capability` (added in twine 5) raises
   326	/// `UnsupportedConfiguration` and refuses to run at all when `--skip-existing`
   327	/// is set against any repository URL other than the public warehouses --
   328	/// confirmed live against a real local `pypiserver`: the upload never reaches
   329	/// the wire. `index: None` means twine's own default target (`.pypirc`'s
   330	/// `pypi` alias, `https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/`), which is always safe.
   331	fn twine_accepts_skip_existing(index: Option<&str>) -> bool {
   332	    match index {
   333	        None => true,
   334	        Some(url) => url.starts_with(PYPI_WAREHOUSE_URL) || url.starts_with(PYPI_TEST_WAREHOUSE_URL),
   335	    }
   336	}

   338	/// Builds the two-step PyPI publish argv sequence: build the sdist and
   339	/// wheel into `dist/`, then upload the exact `dist/<normalized-name>-
   340	/// <version>*` glob via `twine upload`. Both steps run from `package_dir` so
   341	/// `dist/` resolves to that package's own directory in a monorepo, and
   342	/// neither ever builds into or uploads from a fresh temporary directory --
   343	/// `twine`'s own glob targets exactly the artifacts this `python -m build`
   344	/// invocation just produced, not whatever else happens to be sitting in
   345	/// `dist/`.
   346	///
   347	/// `--skip-existing` is included only when `twine_accepts_skip_existing`
   348	/// allows it for `index`; it's mostly redundant for the durable release path
   349	/// anyway, since the operation is only ever dispatched after an `Absent`
   350	/// preflight observation of the exact same registry.
   351	///
   352	/// Package name is normalized to PEP 427 wheel-filename form (lowercased,
   353	/// `-`/`.` -> `_`) before building the glob; `twine` expands the glob
   354	/// internally, so the literal `*` is safe with no shell involved.
   355	/// `index: Some` inserts `--repository-url <url>` before the glob, to target
   356	/// a private index (Nexus/Artifactory PyPI proxy, or a local test registry)
   357	/// instead of public PyPI.
   358	///
   359	/// The build step's interpreter comes from `resolve_python_interpreter` --
   360	/// `python3` first, `python` as a fallback -- rather than a hardcoded
   361	/// `python`, since many systems (macOS, Debian) ship no bare `python`.
   362	pub fn pypi_publish_argv(
   363	    workspace_root: &Path,
   364	    package_dir: &Path,
   365	    package_name: &str,
   366	    version: &Version,
   367	    index: Option<&str>,
   368	) -> Result<Vec<Argv>, GraphError> {
   369	    let interpreter = resolve_python_interpreter(std::env::var_os("PATH").as_deref())?;
   370	    let cwd = workspace_root.join(package_dir);
   371	    let build = Argv {
   372	        program: interpreter.to_string(),
   373	        args: vec![
   374	            "-m".to_string(),
   375	            "build".to_string(),
   376	            "--sdist".to_string(),
   377	            "--wheel".to_string(),
   378	            "--outdir".to_string(),
   379	            "dist/".to_string(),
   380	        ],
   381	        cwd: cwd.clone(),
   382	    };
   383	
   384	    let normalized = normalize_pypi_package_name(package_name);
   385	    let pattern = format!("dist/{normalized}-{}*", version.render());
   386	    let mut upload_args = vec!["upload".to_string()];
   387	    if twine_accepts_skip_existing(index) {
   388	        upload_args.push("--skip-existing".to_string());
   389	    }
   390	    if let Some(idx) = index {
   391	        upload_args.push("--repository-url".to_string());
   392	        upload_args.push(idx.to_string());
   393	    }
   394	    upload_args.push(pattern);
   395	    let upload = Argv {
   396	        program: "twine".to_string(),
   397	        args: upload_args,
   398	        cwd,
   399	    };
   400	
   401	    Ok(vec![build, upload])
   402	}

   404	/// Resolves the interpreter for the PyPI build step's `python -m build`:
   405	/// prefers `python3` -- the only name macOS and Debian systems guarantee --
   406	/// and falls back to bare `python` for systems that only ship that. Errors
   407	/// naming both when neither is on `path_value`.
   408	///
   409	/// `path_value` is injected rather than read from `$PATH` directly so tests
   410	/// can exercise both resolutions and the error without mutating process-wide
   411	/// environment state.
   412	fn resolve_python_interpreter(path_value: Option<&OsStr>) -> Result<&'static str, GraphError> {
   413	    if exists_on_path("python3", path_value) {
   414	        Ok("python3")
   415	    } else if exists_on_path("python", path_value) {
   416	        Ok("python")
   417	    } else {
   418	        Err(GraphError::ReleasePreconditionUnmet {
   419	            requirement: ReleasePreconditionRequirement::PythonInterpreterOnPath,
   420	        })
   421	    }
   422	}

   424	/// Whether `program` exists as a file in some directory of `path_value` --
   425	/// PATH-lookup semantics, without ever spawning it.
   426	fn exists_on_path(program: &str, path_value: Option<&OsStr>) -> bool {
   427	    path_value.is_some_and(|path| std::env::split_paths(path).any(|dir| dir.join(program).is_file()))
   428	}

   432	fn combined_lower(output: &CommandOutput) -> String {
   433	    format!("{}\n{}", output.stdout, output.stderr).to_lowercase()

   436	/// Parses a numeric retry-after value (seconds) as reported by a registry
   437	/// tool's output.
   438	fn parse_retry_after(raw: &str) -> Option<Duration> {
   439	    raw.trim().parse::<u64>().ok().map(Duration::from_secs)
   440	}
   441	
   442	/// Looks for a `retry after <N>` mention in already-lowercased text and
   443	/// parses `<N>` as a whole-second duration.
   444	fn extract_retry_after_duration(text_lower: &str) -> Option<Duration> {
   445	    const NEEDLE: &str = "retry after ";
   446	    let idx = text_lower.find(NEEDLE)?;
   447	    let rest = &text_lower[idx + NEEDLE.len()..];
   448	    let token = rest.split_whitespace().next()?;
   449	    let digits: String = token.chars().take_while(|c| c.is_ascii_digit()).collect();
   450	    if digits.is_empty() {
   451	        return None;
   452	    }
   453	    parse_retry_after(&digits)
   454	}

   456	fn detect_rate_limit(text_lower: &str) -> Option<RegistryError> {
   457	    // Match rate-limit signals with context, never on bare digits alone.
   458	    // Bare "429" in cargo's compressed-size output ("429.1KiB compressed")
   459	    // would otherwise trigger this. Require at least one contextual phrase
   460	    // alongside any "429".
   461	    let is_rate_limited = text_lower.contains("too many requests")
   462	        || text_lower.contains("rate limit")
   463	        || text_lower.contains("erate_limit")
   464	        || (text_lower.contains("429")
   465	            && (text_lower.contains("too many") || text_lower.contains("rate") || text_lower.contains("retry")));
   466	    if is_rate_limited {
   467	        let dur = extract_retry_after_duration(text_lower).unwrap_or(Duration::from_secs(DEFAULT_RATE_LIMIT_WAIT_SECS));
   468	        Some(RegistryError::RateLimited(dur))
   469	    } else {
   470	        None
   471	    }
   472	}
   473	
   474	fn detect_auth_failure(text_lower: &str, raw_stderr: &CommandOutput) -> Option<RegistryError> {
   475	    // Match "401"/"403" with context, never on bare digits alone -- same
   476	    // rationale as detect_rate_limit's guard against bare "429": a byte
   477	    // count or elapsed-time figure in cargo's own packaging/build output
   478	    // ("403129 bytes", "elapsed 4013ms") would otherwise misclassify an
   479	    // unrelated failure as an auth failure.
   480	    if (text_lower.contains("401") && text_lower.contains("auth"))
   481	        || (text_lower.contains("403") && (text_lower.contains("auth") || text_lower.contains("forbidden")))
   482	        || text_lower.contains("authentication")
   483	        || text_lower.contains("not logged in")
   484	        || text_lower.contains("invalid token")
   485	        || text_lower.contains("forbidden")
   486	    {
   487	        Some(RegistryError::AuthFailed(raw_stderr.redacted_stderr()))
   488	    } else {
   489	        None
   490	    }
   491	}

   493	/// Classifies combined `cargo publish` output into a [`PublishOutcome`] or
   494	/// [`RegistryError`].
   495	pub(crate) fn classify_cargo_output(output: &CommandOutput) -> Result<PublishOutcome, RegistryError> {
   496	    let combined = combined_lower(output);
   497	
   498	    if combined.contains("already exists") || combined.contains("already uploaded") {
   499	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished);
   500	    }
   501	    if output.success() {
   502	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::Published);
   503	    }
   504	    if let Some(err) = detect_rate_limit(&combined) {
   505	        return Err(err);
   506	    }
   507	    if let Some(err) = detect_auth_failure(&combined, output) {
   508	        return Err(err);
   509	    }
   510	    Err(RegistryError::Other(format!(
   511	        "cargo publish failed (exit {:?}): {}",
   512	        output.exit_code,
   513	        output.redacted_stderr().trim()
   514	    )))
   515	}

   545	
   546	/// Classifies combined `twine upload` output into a [`PublishOutcome`] or
   547	/// [`RegistryError`].
   548	///
   549	/// Priority order (highest wins):
   550	/// 1. `"already exist"` (from `--skip-existing`) without `"uploading"` ->
   551	///    [`PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished`] (all artifacts skipped). Both
   552	///    phrases present means at least one artifact was freshly uploaded ->
   553	///    `Published`. Handles `dist/` accumulating stale pre-release
   554	///    artifacts: `dist/my_pkg-1.0.0*` matches both `my_pkg-1.0.0a0.whl`
   555	///    (skipped) and `my_pkg-1.0.0.whl` (uploaded), producing mixed output.
   556	///    Only reachable when [`pypi_publish_argv`] included `--skip-existing`
   557	///    (a public-warehouse target); a private-index conflict never emits this
   558	///    text (confirmed live against `pypiserver`: a real conflict there is a
   559	///    bare `409 Conflict`), so it falls through to `RegistryError::Other`
   560	///    below instead -- an intentional fail-closed outcome. The durable
   561	///    release executor only ever calls this after an `Absent` preflight
   562	///    observation of the very same registry, so a private-index conflict
   563	///    here is a rare race, not the common path; a rerun converges through
   564	///    that same observation rather than through this classifier guessing at
   565	///    conflict text with no stable, portable shape across index servers.
   566	/// 2. Zero exit code with no skip-only mention -> [`PublishOutcome::Published`].
   567	/// 3. Rate-limit signal (`429`, `too many requests`, `rate limit`) ->
   568	///    [`RegistryError::RateLimited`] with a parsed or default 60-second
   569	///    retry-after duration.
   570	/// 4. Auth-failure signal (`401`, `403`, `authentication`, etc.) ->
   571	///    [`RegistryError::AuthFailed`].
   572	/// 5. Anything else -> [`RegistryError::Other`].
   573	pub(crate) fn classify_twine_output(output: &CommandOutput) -> Result<PublishOutcome, RegistryError> {
   574	    let combined = combined_lower(output);
   575	
   576	    let has_skip = combined.contains("already exist");
   577	    let has_upload = combined.contains("uploading");
   578	    if has_skip && !has_upload {
   579	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::AlreadyPublished);
   580	    }
   581	    if output.success() {
   582	        return Ok(PublishOutcome::Published);
   583	    }
   584	    if let Some(err) = detect_rate_limit(&combined) {

    48	/// `registry_key` is `Some` only for a non-default registry -- crates.io is
    49	/// the implicit default and never needs `--registry`.
    50	///
    51	/// Before returning, verifies that the on-disk `Cargo.toml` version under
    52	/// `package_dir` (resolving `version.workspace = true` against the
    53	/// workspace root's `[workspace.package].version` when present) matches
    54	/// `version` -- this is the one behavior `SubprocessRegistryClient` had that
    55	/// the durable release executor's own `dispatch_registry` had silently
    56	/// dropped: it catches the common mistake of running `release execute`
    57	/// without first running `callisto version`, which would otherwise silently
    58	/// publish the old on-disk version.
    59	pub fn cargo_publish_argv(
    60	    workspace_root: &Path,
    61	    package_dir: &Path,
    62	    package_name: &str,
    63	    version: &Version,
    64	    registry_key: Option<&str>,
    65	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
    66	    verify_cargo_ondisk_version(workspace_root, package_dir, package_name, version)?;
    67	
    68	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    69	    let mut args = vec![
    70	        "publish".to_string(),
    71	        "--manifest-path".to_string(),
    72	        manifest_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
    73	        "--locked".to_string(),
    74	    ];
    75	    if let Some(reg) = registry_key {
    76	        args.push("--registry".to_string());
    77	        args.push(reg.to_string());
    78	    }
    79	    Ok(Argv {
    80	        program: "cargo".to_string(),
    81	        args,
    82	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
    83	    })
    84	}

    86	fn verify_cargo_ondisk_version(
    87	    workspace_root: &Path,
    88	    package_dir: &Path,
    89	    package_name: &str,
    90	    planned: &Version,
    91	) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
    92	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    93	    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
    94	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
    95	        message: error.to_string(),
    96	    })?;
    97	    // Parse only the [package].version field -- no need for full CST. A
    98	    // permissive `toml::Value` intermediate rather than a direct `String`
    99	    // deserialization, because `version.workspace = true` (Cargo's
   100	    // workspace-version-inheritance syntax) parses `version` as a table, not
   101	    // a string.
   102	    let parsed = toml::from_str::<toml::Value>(&contents).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   103	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
   104	        message: error.to_string(),
   105	    })?;
   106	    let version_value =
   107	        parsed
   108	            .get("package")
   109	            .and_then(|p| p.get("version"))
   110	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   111	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
   112	                message: "missing [package].version".to_string(),
   113	            })?;
   114	
   115	    let on_disk = if let Some(s) = version_value.as_str() {
   116	        s.to_string()
   117	    } else if version_value.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
   118	        let root_manifest_path = workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml");
   119	        let resolver = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_manifest_path)?;
   120	        let ws_version = resolver
   121	            .workspace_version()?
   122	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   123	                path: root_manifest_path.clone(),
   124	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but the workspace root has no [workspace.package].version"
   125	                    .to_string(),
   126	            })?;
   127	        ws_version.render().to_string()
   128	    } else {
   129	        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   130	            path: manifest_path,
   131	            message: "[package].version is neither a string nor a `{ workspace = true }` table".to_string(),
   132	        });
   133	    };
   134	
   135	    let found = Version::parse(&on_disk, planned.grammar())?;
   136	    if found != *planned {
   137	        return Err(GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift {
   138	            package: PackageId::Prefixed {
   139	                ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo,
   140	                name: package_name.to_string(),
   141	            },
   142	            expected: planned.clone(),
   143	            found,
   144	        });
   145	    }
   146	    Ok(())
   147	}

   151	/// The npm-compatible package manager a workspace uses, detected from
   152	/// lockfile presence. Each one needs a materially different invocation to
   153	/// publish a single named package out of a monorepo -- see
   154	/// [`npm_publish_argv`].
   155	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   156	pub enum NpmPackageManager {
   157	    Pnpm,
   158	    Yarn,
   159	    Bun,
   160	    Npm,
   161	}
   162	
   163	/// Detects the npm-compatible package manager for `workspace_root` from
   164	/// lockfile presence. Detection priority: pnpm > yarn > bun > npm (default).
   165	///
   166	/// This is real, live-today correctness content: the durable release
   167	/// executor's `dispatch_registry` used to hardcode plain `npm publish`
   168	/// regardless of which package manager a workspace actually uses, so a pnpm
   169	/// or yarn workspace published with the wrong tool.
   170	pub fn detect_npm_package_manager(workspace_root: &Path) -> NpmPackageManager {
   171	    if workspace_root.join("pnpm-lock.yaml").exists() {
   172	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm
   173	    } else if workspace_root.join("yarn.lock").exists() {
   174	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn
   175	    } else if workspace_root.join("bun.lockb").exists() || workspace_root.join("bun.lock").exists() {
   176	        // bun.lockb is the legacy binary lockfile format; bun.lock (text) is
   177	        // written by Bun >= 1.1.1. Both signal a bun-managed workspace.
   178	        NpmPackageManager::Bun
   179	    } else {
   180	        NpmPackageManager::Npm
   181	    }
   182	}
   183	
   184	/// Builds the npm-ecosystem publish argv for one package, given the
   185	/// already-detected `package_manager` (see [`detect_npm_package_manager`]).
   186	///
   187	/// | Package manager | Program | Base args                                  |
   188	/// |------------------|---------|--------------------------------------------|
   189	/// | Pnpm             | `pnpm`  | `publish --filter=<name> --no-git-checks`  |
   190	/// | Yarn             | `yarn`  | `workspace <name> npm publish`             |
   191	/// | Bun              | `bun`   | `publish` (run from `package_dir`)         |
   192	/// | Npm              | `npm`   | `publish --workspace=<name>`               |
   193	///
   194	/// `--filter=`/`--workspace=` use the joined form so the name cannot be
   195	/// re-read as an option. Yarn takes the name positionally and has no joined
   196	/// spelling, so there it rests on `ReleasePackageId`'s leading-`-` rejection.
   197	///
   198	/// `tag`/`access`/`registry` are appended to every variant's base args.
   199	/// `package_dir` is only used for bun: it has no `--filter`/`--workspace`
   200	/// flag to target one package by name, so it alone must run from the
   201	/// package's own directory rather than the workspace root.
   202	pub fn npm_publish_argv(
   203	    workspace_root: &Path,
   204	    package_dir: &Path,
   205	    package_name: &str,
   206	    package_manager: NpmPackageManager,
   207	    tag: Option<&str>,
   208	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   209	    registry: Option<&str>,
   210	) -> Argv {
   211	    let extra = npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry);
   212	
   213	    let (program, mut args, cwd) = match package_manager {
   214	        NpmPackageManager::Pnpm => (
   215	            "pnpm",
   216	            vec![
   217	                "publish".to_string(),
   218	                // `--filter=<name>`, not `--filter <name>`: the joined form
   219	                // cannot be re-read as an option even if a name slipped past
   220	                // `ReleasePackageId`'s charset rule.
   221	                format!("--filter={package_name}"),
   222	                // pnpm >= 7 refuses to publish from a dirty working tree by
   223	                // default. After `callisto version` stages manifest bumps,
   224	                // the tree is always dirty until the operator commits, so
   225	                // this bypasses the git-status check.
   226	                "--no-git-checks".to_string(),
   227	            ],
   228	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   229	        ),
   230	        NpmPackageManager::Yarn => (
   231	            "yarn",
   232	            vec![
   233	                "workspace".to_string(),
   234	                package_name.to_string(),
   235	                "npm".to_string(),
   236	                "publish".to_string(),
   237	            ],
   238	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   239	        ),
   240	        NpmPackageManager::Bun => ("bun", vec!["publish".to_string()], workspace_root.join(package_dir)),
   241	        NpmPackageManager::Npm => (
   242	            "npm",
   243	            vec!["publish".to_string(), format!("--workspace={package_name}")],
   244	            workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   245	        ),
   246	    };
   247	    args.extend(extra);
   248	    Argv {
   249	        program: program.to_string(),
   250	        args,
   251	        cwd,
   252	    }
   253	}

   255	/// The access an npm package publishes with: the explicit `publishConfig.access`,
   256	/// else `public` for a scoped `@scope/name` (npm defaults scoped packages to restricted).
   257	pub fn npm_default_access(name: &str, explicit: Option<NpmAccess>) -> Option<NpmAccess> {
   258	    explicit.or_else(|| name.starts_with('@').then_some(NpmAccess::Public))
   259	}
   260	
   261	/// `--tag`/`--access`/`--registry`, shared by every npm-ecosystem publish argv.
   262	fn npm_publish_flags(
   263	    package_name: &str,
   264	    tag: Option<&str>,
   265	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   266	    registry: Option<&str>,
   267	) -> Vec<String> {
   268	    let mut extra: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
   269	    if let Some(t) = tag {
   270	        extra.push("--tag".to_string());
   271	        extra.push(t.to_string());
   272	    }
   273	    if let Some(access) = npm_default_access(package_name, access) {
   274	        extra.push("--access".to_string());
   275	        extra.push(
   276	            match access {
   277	                NpmAccess::Public => "public",
   278	                NpmAccess::Restricted => "restricted",
   279	            }
   280	            .to_string(),
   281	        );
   282	    }
   283	    if let Some(reg) = registry {
   284	        extra.push("--registry".to_string());
   285	        extra.push(reg.to_string());
   286	    }
   287	    extra
   288	}

   290	/// Publishes the package in `package_dir` by path: `npm publish <dir>` from the
   291	/// workspace root, whatever the package manager. pnpm `--filter`, yarn
   292	/// `workspace`, and npm `--workspace` select only workspace members, and an npm
   293	/// platform package directory usually is not one. The path is absolute, so it
   294	/// cannot be read as an option.
   295	pub fn npm_publish_directory_argv(
   296	    workspace_root: &Path,
   297	    package_dir: &Path,
   298	    package_name: &str,
   299	    tag: Option<&str>,
   300	    access: Option<NpmAccess>,
   301	    registry: Option<&str>,
   302	) -> Argv {
   303	    let mut args = vec![
   304	        "publish".to_string(),
   305	        workspace_root.join(package_dir).to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
   306	    ];
   307	    args.extend(npm_publish_flags(package_name, tag, access, registry));
   308	    Argv {
   309	        program: "npm".to_string(),
   310	        args,
   311	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
   312	    }
   313	}

   317	/// The public warehouses twine (>= 5) allows `--skip-existing` against.
   318	/// Matches twine's own `repository.WAREHOUSE`/`repository.TEST_WAREHOUSE`
   319	/// constants exactly, including the `upload.` subdomain -- PyPI's upload
   320	/// endpoint, not its browsing/simple-index host (`pypi.org`).
   321	const PYPI_WAREHOUSE_URL: &str = "https://upload.pypi.org/";
   322	const PYPI_TEST_WAREHOUSE_URL: &str = "https://test.pypi.org/";
   323	
   324	/// Whether twine accepts `--skip-existing` for this upload target. Twine's
   325	/// own `verify_feature_capability` (added in twine 5) raises
   326	/// `UnsupportedConfiguration` and refuses to run at all when `--skip-existing`
   327	/// is set against any repository URL other than the public warehouses --
   328	/// confirmed live against a real local `pypiserver`: the upload never reaches
   329	/// the wire. `index: None` means twine's own default target (`.pypirc`'s
   330	/// `pypi` alias, `https://upload.pypi.org/legacy/`), which is always safe.
   331	fn twine_accepts_skip_existing(index: Option<&str>) -> bool {
   332	    match index {
   333	        None => true,
   334	        Some(url) => url.starts_with(PYPI_WAREHOUSE_URL) || url.starts_with(PYPI_TEST_WAREHOUSE_URL),
   335	    }
   336	}

   338	/// Builds the two-step PyPI publish argv sequence: build the sdist and
   339	/// wheel into `dist/`, then upload the exact `dist/<normalized-name>-
   340	/// <version>*` glob via `twine upload`. Both steps run from `package_dir` so
   341	/// `dist/` resolves to that package's own directory in a monorepo, and
   342	/// neither ever builds into or uploads from a fresh temporary directory --
   343	/// `twine`'s own glob targets exactly the artifacts this `python -m build`
   344	/// invocation just produced, not whatever else happens to be sitting in
   345	/// `dist/`.
   346	///
   347	/// `--skip-existing` is included only when `twine_accepts_skip_existing`
   348	/// allows it for `index`; it's mostly redundant for the durable release path
   349	/// anyway, since the operation is only ever dispatched after an `Absent`
   350	/// preflight observation of the exact same registry.
   351	///
   352	/// Package name is normalized to PEP 427 wheel-filename form (lowercased,
   353	/// `-`/`.` -> `_`) before building the glob; `twine` expands the glob
   354	/// internally, so the literal `*` is safe with no shell involved.
   355	/// `index: Some` inserts `--repository-url <url>` before the glob, to target
   356	/// a private index (Nexus/Artifactory PyPI proxy, or a local test registry)
   357	/// instead of public PyPI.
   358	///
   359	/// The build step's interpreter comes from `resolve_python_interpreter` --
   360	/// `python3` first, `python` as a fallback -- rather than a hardcoded
   361	/// `python`, since many systems (macOS, Debian) ship no bare `python`.
   362	pub fn pypi_publish_argv(
   363	    workspace_root: &Path,
   364	    package_dir: &Path,
   365	    package_name: &str,
   366	    version: &Version,
   367	    index: Option<&str>,
   368	) -> Result<Vec<Argv>, GraphError> {
   369	    let interpreter = resolve_python_interpreter(std::env::var_os("PATH").as_deref())?;
   370	    let cwd = workspace_root.join(package_dir);
   371	    let build = Argv {
   372	        program: interpreter.to_string(),
   373	        args: vec![
   374	            "-m".to_string(),
   375	            "build".to_string(),
   376	            "--sdist".to_string(),
   377	            "--wheel".to_string(),
   378	            "--outdir".to_string(),
   379	            "dist/".to_string(),
   380	        ],
   381	        cwd: cwd.clone(),
   382	    };
   383	
   384	    let normalized = normalize_pypi_package_name(package_name);
   385	    let pattern = format!("dist/{normalized}-{}*", version.render());
   386	    let mut upload_args = vec!["upload".to_string()];
   387	    if twine_accepts_skip_existing(index) {
   388	        upload_args.push("--skip-existing".to_string());
   389	    }
   390	    if let Some(idx) = index {
   391	        upload_args.push("--repository-url".to_string());
   392	        upload_args.push(idx.to_string());
   393	    }
   394	    upload_args.push(pattern);
   395	    let upload = Argv {
   396	        program: "twine".to_string(),
   397	        args: upload_args,
   398	        cwd,
   399	    };
   400	
   401	    Ok(vec![build, upload])
   402	}

    44	/// Builds the exact `cargo publish` argv for one crate: `--manifest-path`
    45	/// (so the caller can keep the workspace root as its own working directory)
    46	/// plus `--locked`, so a stale `Cargo.lock` fails the publish immediately
    47	/// instead of `cargo` silently re-resolving one at publish time.
    48	/// `registry_key` is `Some` only for a non-default registry -- crates.io is
    49	/// the implicit default and never needs `--registry`.
    50	///
    51	/// Before returning, verifies that the on-disk `Cargo.toml` version under
    52	/// `package_dir` (resolving `version.workspace = true` against the
    53	/// workspace root's `[workspace.package].version` when present) matches
    54	/// `version` -- this is the one behavior `SubprocessRegistryClient` had that
    55	/// the durable release executor's own `dispatch_registry` had silently
    56	/// dropped: it catches the common mistake of running `release execute`
    57	/// without first running `callisto version`, which would otherwise silently
    58	/// publish the old on-disk version.
    59	pub fn cargo_publish_argv(
    60	    workspace_root: &Path,
    61	    package_dir: &Path,
    62	    package_name: &str,
    63	    version: &Version,
    64	    registry_key: Option<&str>,
    65	) -> Result<Argv, GraphError> {
    66	    verify_cargo_ondisk_version(workspace_root, package_dir, package_name, version)?;
    67	
    68	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    69	    let mut args = vec![
    70	        "publish".to_string(),
    71	        "--manifest-path".to_string(),
    72	        manifest_path.to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
    73	        "--locked".to_string(),
    74	    ];
    75	    if let Some(reg) = registry_key {
    76	        args.push("--registry".to_string());
    77	        args.push(reg.to_string());
    78	    }
    79	    Ok(Argv {
    80	        program: "cargo".to_string(),
    81	        args,
    82	        cwd: workspace_root.to_path_buf(),
    83	    })
    84	}

    86	fn verify_cargo_ondisk_version(
    87	    workspace_root: &Path,
    88	    package_dir: &Path,
    89	    package_name: &str,
    90	    planned: &Version,
    91	) -> Result<(), GraphError> {
    92	    let manifest_path = workspace_root.join(package_dir).join("Cargo.toml");
    93	    let contents = std::fs::read_to_string(&manifest_path).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
    94	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
    95	        message: error.to_string(),
    96	    })?;
    97	    // Parse only the [package].version field -- no need for full CST. A
    98	    // permissive `toml::Value` intermediate rather than a direct `String`
    99	    // deserialization, because `version.workspace = true` (Cargo's
   100	    // workspace-version-inheritance syntax) parses `version` as a table, not
   101	    // a string.
   102	    let parsed = toml::from_str::<toml::Value>(&contents).map_err(|error| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   103	        path: manifest_path.clone(),
   104	        message: error.to_string(),
   105	    })?;
   106	    let version_value =
   107	        parsed
   108	            .get("package")
   109	            .and_then(|p| p.get("version"))
   110	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   111	                path: manifest_path.clone(),
   112	                message: "missing [package].version".to_string(),
   113	            })?;
   114	
   115	    let on_disk = if let Some(s) = version_value.as_str() {
   116	        s.to_string()
   117	    } else if version_value.get("workspace").and_then(toml::Value::as_bool) == Some(true) {
   118	        let root_manifest_path = workspace_root.join("Cargo.toml");
   119	        let resolver = WorkspaceCargoResolver::load(&root_manifest_path)?;
   120	        let ws_version = resolver
   121	            .workspace_version()?
   122	            .ok_or_else(|| GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   123	                path: root_manifest_path.clone(),
   124	                message: "`version.workspace = true` but the workspace root has no [workspace.package].version"
   125	                    .to_string(),
   126	            })?;
   127	        ws_version.render().to_string()
   128	    } else {
   129	        return Err(GraphError::ReleaseInputRead {
   130	            path: manifest_path,
   131	            message: "[package].version is neither a string nor a `{ workspace = true }` table".to_string(),
   132	        });
   133	    };
   134	
   135	    let found = Version::parse(&on_disk, planned.grammar())?;
   136	    if found != *planned {
   137	        return Err(GraphError::OnDiskVersionDrift {
   138	            package: PackageId::Prefixed {
   139	                ecosystem: Ecosystem::Cargo,
   140	                name: package_name.to_string(),
   141	            },
   142	            expected: planned.clone(),
   143	            found,
   144	        });
   145	    }
   146	    Ok(())
   147	}

        let doc = parse(&config);

        assert_eq!(release_table["product-package"].as_str(), Some("cargo/app"));
        assert_eq!(release_table["forge-repository"].as_str(), Some("example/tools"));
        let assets: Vec<(&str, &str, &str)> = release_table["artifact"]
            .as_array()
            .unwrap()
            .iter()
            .map(|artifact| {
                (
                    artifact["package"].as_str().unwrap(),
                    artifact["target"].as_str().unwrap(),
                    artifact["asset-name"].as_str().unwrap(),

        assert_eq!(

docs/releasing.md:26:`callisto init --workflow` (or answering yes to its prompt) writes `.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`. That path is what `release plan` binds artifact attestations to — keep the name if you rename anything else.
docs/releasing.md:32:- **Build-matrix shape** (artifact slots or napi platform packages): `version-pr`, then `plan` -> `build` -> `execute`.
docs/releasing.md:34:  - `build` has one matrix job per napi target from `callisto matrix` and one per artifact slot, and attests the slot assets.
docs/releasing.md:35:  - `execute` places the napi builds (`napi artifacts`), writes the artifact manifest, and runs `callisto release execute`.
docs/releasing.md:36:- Maturin builds, and platform packages without `napi.targets`, get no generated workflow.
docs/releasing.md:40:Limits of the build-matrix shape:
docs/releasing.md:42:- `napi build` runs in the napi package's directory. When the addon crate lives elsewhere (for example `packages/napi` with the crate in `crates/binding`), the step passes `--manifest-path` for the workspace crate whose lib name equals `napi.binaryName`; `callisto matrix` fails with E204 when no single crate matches.
docs/releasing.md:44:- Artifact slots build the package's `bin` targets with `cargo build --release --locked`. Any other build (a `cdylib`, custom features) needs a hand-edited step.
docs/releasing.md:60:Callisto treats the verified merge of the release PR as the authorization and has no approval step of its own; any extra gate is your CI's choice. Keep registry credentials scoped only to the `execute` job, so planning and build jobs cannot read them. Only `execute` may receive `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`, `NPM_TOKEN`, or `TWINE_PASSWORD` — never at workflow scope, in build jobs, or in an action input.
docs/releasing.md:64:Progress is derived from provider observation (registry, remote tag, forge release, assets); binary assets publish to the GitHub Release. A green workflow is not by itself proof a release exists — use the release receipt and independent provider checks as completion evidence.
docs/releasing.md:66:`callisto-action` has two modes: `mode: version-pr` (default) opens or updates the release PR; `mode: release` installs callisto and runs `callisto release`. Its former `publish` and `create_github_release` inputs are ignored. Workspaces with artifact slots or platform packages release through the plan/build/execute workflow instead.
docs/releasing.md:113:The orchestration revision is the SHA of the run itself (`github.sha`), never the moving tip of `main`, because attestations are stamped with the run's SHA. The release path runs on `main` only. A recovery dispatch is gated by `recovery-checks` (credential-free release workflow contract and policy checks), not the full `verify` job, so an unrelated failure on `main` cannot block publishing an already-merged release.
docs/releasing.md:117:Every run is the same kind of run.
docs/releasing.md:127:`[release].forge-repository` in `callisto.toml` is the one GitHub forge destination. Planning rejects an `--artifact-repository` that differs from it, execution rejects an intent whose artifact slots target another repository, and a `[release]` without it fails before writing an intent. A legacy `[release.profiles.production].forge-repository` is still read when the top-level key is absent, for migration only; any other profile name is rejected.
docs/releasing.md:164:- **Cargo**: `cargo info NAME@VERSION --registry REGISTRY`, run from the source workspace root so `.cargo/config.toml` registry definitions and credentials apply (`--registry` is never omitted). Exit 0 with a matching `version:` line is exact evidence; exit 101 with ``could not find `NAME@VERSION` `` is absence; anything else (including an unreachable registry) is indeterminate and retried. A yanked version reads as absent, because `cargo info` cannot see yanks — that fails closed: the registry refuses the publish that follows, and the run ends in a typed unconfirmed-publication error rather than a receipt.
docs/releasing.md:168:Registry endpoints must be `https` — no loopback exception, since an endpoint receives a credential.
docs/releasing.md:178:GitHub Actions schedules jobs, supplies two isolated checkouts, transports artifacts, and injects credentials only into `execute`. Callisto owns source validation, provenance, plan derivation, provider observation, transition selection, terminality, receipt creation, and artifact validation. Workflow shell must not reimplement those semantics.
docs/releasing.md:180:All transient intent, receipt, downloaded artifacts, and build output live under `RUNNER_TEMP`, not inside a source checkout. Build and plan have no registry credentials or provider-write token.
docs/releasing.md:186:Each asset's GitHub provenance is bound to the current coordinator workflow revision — the revision GitHub records for the workflow run. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# Regression test for the github.action_ref -> callisto@<version> resolution
     3	# in scripts/install-callisto.sh: a workflow pinned to
     4	# `callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@X.Y.Z` (or setup-callisto the same way)
     5	# must install X.Y.Z, not whatever GitHub Releases calls "latest". Extracts
     6	# the snippet by real text anchors so this test always exercises the
     7	# script's current logic.
     8	set -u
     9	ACTION_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
    10	INSTALL_SCRIPT="$ACTION_DIR/scripts/install-callisto.sh"
    11	
    12	extract_snippet() {
    13	  sed -n '/^TAG_NAME="\$INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION"$/,/^# Validate verification mode$/p' "$INSTALL_SCRIPT" \
    14	    | sed '$d'
    15	}
    16	
    17	# Runs the extracted snippet with INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION/GITHUB_ACTION_REF set
    18	# and `git ls-remote` stubbed to print tag_lines; prints the resulting
    19	# TAG_NAME and records every git invocation.
    20	run_case() {
    21	  local input_version="$1" action_ref="$2" tag_lines="$3"
    22	  local tmp_script calls_file
    23	  tmp_script="$(mktemp)"
    24	  calls_file="$(mktemp)"
    25	  {
    26	    printf 'git() { echo "git $*" >> %q; if [[ "$1 $2" == "ls-remote --tags" ]]; then printf %%s %q; fi; }\n' \
    27	      "$calls_file" "$tag_lines"
    28	    printf 'INPUT_CALLISTO_VERSION=%q\n' "$input_version"
    29	    [[ -n "$action_ref" ]] && printf 'GITHUB_ACTION_REF=%q\n' "$action_ref"
    30	    printf 'INPUT_CALLISTO_SOURCE=auto\n'
    31	    extract_snippet
    32	    printf 'echo "TAG_NAME=$TAG_NAME"\n'
    33	  } > "$tmp_script"
    34	  bash "$tmp_script"
    35	  echo "---CALLS---"
    36	  cat "$calls_file"
    37	  rm -f "$tmp_script" "$calls_file"
    38	}
    39	
    40	fail=0
    41	TAGS=$'deadbeef00000000000000000000000000000001\trefs/tags/callisto@0.7.0\nabc1230000000000000000000000000000000002\trefs/tags/callisto@0.8.0\nabc1230000000000000000000000000000000002\trefs/tags/callisto@0.8.0^{}\n'
    42	
    43	# 1. No action ref set (local/unpinned invocation): stays "latest", no git call.
    44	out=$(run_case "latest" "" "$TAGS")
    45	if [[ "$out" != *"TAG_NAME=latest"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"git ls-remote"* ]]; then
    46	  echo "FAIL test_no_action_ref_stays_latest_without_git_call: $out"; fail=1
    47	else
    48	  echo "PASS test_no_action_ref_stays_latest_without_git_call"
    49	fi
    50	
    51	# 2. Action ref matches a published callisto@ tag: resolved, dereferenced ^{} ignored.
    52	out=$(run_case "latest" "abc1230000000000000000000000000000000002" "$TAGS")
    53	if [[ "$out" != *"TAG_NAME=callisto@0.8.0"* ]]; then
    54	  echo "FAIL test_matching_action_ref_resolves_to_tag: $out"; fail=1
    55	else
    56	  echo "PASS test_matching_action_ref_resolves_to_tag"
    57	fi
    58	
    59	# 3. Action ref matches no tag: falls back to true latest.
    60	out=$(run_case "latest" "0000000000000000000000000000000000000f" "$TAGS")
    61	if [[ "$out" != *"TAG_NAME=latest"* ]]; then
    62	  echo "FAIL test_unmatched_action_ref_falls_back_to_latest: $out"; fail=1
    63	else
    64	  echo "PASS test_unmatched_action_ref_falls_back_to_latest"
    65	fi
    66	
    67	# 4. Explicit version override is never touched, even with a resolvable action ref.
    68	out=$(run_case "callisto@0.5.0" "abc1230000000000000000000000000000000002" "$TAGS")
    69	if [[ "$out" != *"TAG_NAME=callisto@0.5.0"* ]] || [[ "$out" == *"git ls-remote"* ]]; then
    70	  echo "FAIL test_explicit_version_override_skips_resolution: $out"; fail=1
    71	else
    72	  echo "PASS test_explicit_version_override_skips_resolution"
    73	fi
    74	
    75	exit "$fail"

Author: Gabe Castro <gabe@techworx.dev>
Date:   Sat Sep 26 20:00:44 2026 +0000

    fix(init): generated workflows work and stay pinned (#163)
    
    * fix(action): install the callisto version the action is pinned to
    
    setup-callisto and callisto-action defaulted to GitHub Releases' 'latest',
    so a workflow pinned to callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@0.8.0 could
    silently install a newer or older CLI than its own commit. Resolve
    github.action_ref against orin-dx/callisto's callisto@ tags first, falling
    back to true latest only when the ref is unset or unresolvable; an explicit
    version input still overrides.
    
    * fix(init): generated workflow targets the real default branch
    
    callisto-action defaults its `branch` input to `main`, so a generated
    workflow that never sets it opens the release PR against `main` even
    on a trunk repo. Pass the detected branch explicitly.
    
    default_branch also silently fell back to `main` whenever local
    origin/HEAD was unset, which is the common case for a shallow or
    hand-built clone. Try origin/HEAD, then a live query of origin, then
    the checked-out branch, before falling back, and report which source
    resolved it.
    
    * fix(init): validate flags up front, list every written file, and work without origin
    
    - --forge-repository/--product-package were silently dropped instead of
      rejected when --artifact-target wasn't given; validate all flags together
      now, before any facts are even detected.
    - InitReport gains `files`, so --dry-run (and --format json) reports every
      file init would write, including the generated workflow and
      .changeset/README.md, not just callisto.toml.
    - init no longer refuses without an `origin` remote: it writes the config,
      skips the workflow and shipping-binaries questions with a warning
      diagnostic, and lets `callisto release` refuse later when one is needed.
    - Drop SECURITY.md's hardcoded current version, which goes stale on release.
    
    Amends CLI-INIT-09 and CLI-INIT-12; removes the now-unreachable E192 in
    favor of two new flag-validation codes (E298, E299).
    
    * test(schema): accept the init-origin-missing diagnostic code
    
    The init change added a warning code; the schema guard pins the variant set deliberately.

Author: Gabe Castro <gabe@techworx.dev>
Date:   Fri Sep 25 19:54:34 2026 +0000

    refactor!: let tools own auth; one build; lighter release and init (#143)
    
    * refactor(release)!: drop the local credential pre-flight
    
    cargo, npm, twine and gh report their own auth failures, and a rerun adopts every effect that already landed, so a second credential model in Callisto only drifts from the tools'.
    
    * refactor(release)!: write a local receipt only with --receipt
    
    A default per-user receipt location needed repo hashing, path canonicalization and a platform state-dir table for a file nobody asked for; the summary on stdout (or JSON receipt with --format json) covers the local case.
    
    * refactor(init)!: stop validating artifact targets against rustc
    
    The rustc target list lags custom and newer triples and made init depend on the host toolchain; the build that uses a triple reports an unknown one precisely. Empty and repeated triples are still refused.
    
    * ci: run real-registry e2e tests on Linux only
    
    Installing Verdaccio and pypiserver on macOS needed Python 3.13 and reverse-DNS workarounds for coverage the Linux leg already gives; the tests compile out elsewhere.
    
    * build!: remove cargo features; one build for tests and release
    
    The ecosystem features gated nothing a user could meaningfully turn off, and the inference feature made the shipped binary differ from the tested one. Every ecosystem and commit inference are now always compiled in; release-trigger already decides at runtime which packages infer.

    refactor!: let tools own auth; one build; lighter release and init (#143)
    
    * refactor(release)!: drop the local credential pre-flight
    
    cargo, npm, twine and gh report their own auth failures, and a rerun adopts every effect that already landed, so a second credential model in Callisto only drifts from the tools'.
    
    * refactor(release)!: write a local receipt only with --receipt
    
    A default per-user receipt location needed repo hashing, path canonicalization and a platform state-dir table for a file nobody asked for; the summary on stdout (or JSON receipt with --format json) covers the local case.
    
    * refactor(init)!: stop validating artifact targets against rustc
    
    The rustc target list lags custom and newer triples and made init depend on the host toolchain; the build that uses a triple reports an unknown one precisely. Empty and repeated triples are still refused.
    
    * ci: run real-registry e2e tests on Linux only
    
    Installing Verdaccio and pypiserver on macOS needed Python 3.13 and reverse-DNS workarounds for coverage the Linux leg already gives; the tests compile out elsewhere.
    
    * build!: remove cargo features; one build for tests and release
    
    The ecosystem features gated nothing a user could meaningfully turn off, and the inference feature made the shipped binary differ from the tested one. Every ecosystem and commit inference are now always compiled in; release-trigger already decides at runtime which packages infer.

Author: Gabe Castro <gabe@techworx.dev>
Date:   Sat Sep 26 20:00:44 2026 +0000

    fix(init): generated workflows work and stay pinned (#163)
    
    * fix(action): install the callisto version the action is pinned to
    
    setup-callisto and callisto-action defaulted to GitHub Releases' 'latest',
    so a workflow pinned to callisto-action@<sha> # callisto@0.8.0 could
    silently install a newer or older CLI than its own commit. Resolve
    github.action_ref against orin-dx/callisto's callisto@ tags first, falling
    back to true latest only when the ref is unset or unresolvable; an explicit
    version input still overrides.
    
    * fix(init): generated workflow targets the real default branch
    
    callisto-action defaults its `branch` input to `main`, so a generated
    workflow that never sets it opens the release PR against `main` even
    on a trunk repo. Pass the detected branch explicitly.
    
    default_branch also silently fell back to `main` whenever local
    origin/HEAD was unset, which is the common case for a shallow or
    hand-built clone. Try origin/HEAD, then a live query of origin, then
    the checked-out branch, before falling back, and report which source
    resolved it.
    
    * fix(init): validate flags up front, list every written file, and work without origin
    
    - --forge-repository/--product-package were silently dropped instead of
      rejected when --artifact-target wasn't given; validate all flags together
      now, before any facts are even detected.
    - InitReport gains `files`, so --dry-run (and --format json) reports every
      file init would write, including the generated workflow and
      .changeset/README.md, not just callisto.toml.
    - init no longer refuses without an `origin` remote: it writes the config,
      skips the workflow and shipping-binaries questions with a warning
      diagnostic, and lets `callisto release` refuse later when one is needed.
    - Drop SECURITY.md's hardcoded current version, which goes stale on release.
    
    Amends CLI-INIT-09 and CLI-INIT-12; removes the now-unreachable E192 in
    favor of two new flag-validation codes (E298, E299).
    
    * test(schema): accept the init-origin-missing diagnostic code
    
    The init change added a warning code; the schema guard pins the variant set deliberately.
